articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Engaging with the Myanmar junta is a short-sighted move

Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured

The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself . Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: United stand: On protests against SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Protests against SIR are a recognition that it could subvert popular will

The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.

The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. The call for the restoration of institutional integrity is the need of the hour; but Mr. Gandhi must be careful not to misstate the nature of the crisis. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.keyPoints:
• Protests against SIR are a recognition that it could subvert popular will
• The gathering of hundreds of thousands of people at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, organised by the Congress-led INDIA bloc parties, was a milestone in the battle for the restoration of the integrity of India’s election process. As more and more skeletons tumble out the of the closet of the Election Commission of India (ECI), its chief Gyanesh Kumar has chosen silence while the ruling BJP has rushed to shield him from criticism. The united outcry of protest by the Opposition, led by the Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi , is a strong signal of public opinion for the ruling party and India’s institutions, including the ECI, that appear complicit in a scheme that threatens the foundations of Indian democracy. What remains unexplained by the ECI and Mr. Kumar are malpractices in the Special Intensive Revision that could have the effect of subverting the popular will. Protestors on Sunday had arrived from all parts of India, and included people directly affected by the SIR across the country.
• The protest reinforced Mr. Gandhi’s central role as the key challenger of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Gandhi, for all his faults, has been an uncompromising champion of constitutional values and pluralism in India. The BJP caricatured him, and even non-BJP voices had bought into the idea of Mr. Gandhi being a privileged dynast out of touch with the commoner. While his ancestry is a matter of fact, so is his tenacity. All Opposition parties mobilised for the protest, but the centrality of the Congress party was unmistakable. Mr. Gandhi has a special focus on subaltern classes to be included in positions of responsibility in the party. The Sunday protest was clearly the largest show of strength in recent memory. The manner in which the Congress coordinated with the wide spectrum of the Opposition, often involving rivals in States, also indicates a clear sense of purpose and pragmatism. In his well-reasoned call for accountability of the ECI, Mr. Gandhi ended up questioning the legitimacy of the previous election without providing any substantive basis for his allegations. He must remember that his emergence as the voice of the Opposition places on him the responsibility of being measured in his speeches and his steps.

articles.title: Cascading effect: On dams and land rights
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must respect land rights of its people while building dams

The bureaucratic impetus for the 11.2-GW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) in Arunachal Pradesh purportedly comes from China’s aggressive development of a 60-GW mega-dam in Tibet , stoking anxieties among Indian authorities over ‘weaponised’ transboundary waters. Beijing may be able to divert flows in the Yarlung Tsangpo river, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India, to cause drought downstream or release water en masse to trigger catastrophic floods in Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. New Delhi thus imagines SUMP as a strategic buffer, but in so doing faces a dilemma it should not attempt to resolve with force. Its extant top-down approach, exemplified by deploying security forces to guard survey teams and imposing the State Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act against activists, only validates fears among locals that the state will grab their land. The region also hosts sustained protests against the Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project , expanding the indictment to Arunachal Pradesh’s model of hydroelectric power development. The eastern Himalayas are among the most tectonically active and erosion-prone landscapes in the world. The mega-dam in Tibet will comprise five cascading power stations over the river’s roughly 2,000-metre fall over 50 km. Beijing has maintained the dam will not harm countries downstream but has declined to share crucial engineering details. This is why diplomacy will be an essential part of operating SUMP, in addition to Beijing’s disputed claims on Arunachal Pradesh.

The Brahmaputra basin in Assam and Bangladesh receives most of its water from monsoon rains and tributaries downstream of the Tibetan Plateau, so China cannot straightforwardly control the river’s total flow through India. Yet since Chinese interventions would have greater consequences closer to the border, SUMP will need information about both the mega-dam’s operations and downstream inflows to plan its own operations, and Beijing has declined to share the former. SUMP thus faces many uncertainties at the outset. Despite India repeatedly raising the issue with China at the highest levels, headway has been limited to Beijing agreeing to share hydrological data on humanitarian grounds during emergencies. Planners have contemplated maintaining the SUMP reservoir at 70% to accommodate unexpected surges, but the level of protection possible if China supplies no advance warning remains unclear. This uncertainty is a thorn in the side of the government’s push against more legitimate resistance by Adi community members and civil rights groups. The need for the project does not excuse the state from following all the relevant laws and protections. The state cannot protect the nation’s needs by antagonising the nation’s people.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India and the world must stand up against the bullying of Cuba by the U.S.

Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 28, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: 60-day long prohibitive orders passed ‘ex-parte’ to prevent unrest in key capital zones: Delhi Police in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests witnessed violence in New Delhi district; one of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24

Seven separate prohibitive orders passed by the Delhi Police under Section 163 Bharatiya Nagarik Duraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the national capital show restrictions concerning free movement were imposed way before protests erupted demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests against alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks witnessed violence in New Delhi district, the power and commercial heart of the capital city. One of them imposes prohibitions from September 26 to November 24.

The prohibitive orders are for a maximum period of 60 days, till the latter half of October. They are ex-parte or without hearing any objections, saying “notice cannot be served individually on all concerned”.

The orders, which are part of an affidavit filed by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar in the Supreme Court, said “reports have been received indicate that such conditions now exists that unrestricted holding of public meetings, processions/demonstrations, etc, in the area are likely to cause obstruction to traffic, danger to human safety and disturbance of public tranquility”.
The police reasoned in the orders that it was necessary to take “speedy measures” to “prevent danger to human life or safety and disturbance to public tranquility”.

The seven orders comprise the police sub-divisions of Connaught Place, Tughlak Road, Parliament Street, Chanakya Puri — where the Prime Minister’s residence, Rashtrapati Bhavan, foreign embassies, and other vital installations are located — Barakhamba Road, Safdarjung Enclave in south-west Delhi, and Defence Colony.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Anti-CEC protest fallout: Supreme Court issues fresh directions to Centre, Delhi Police

The orders prohibited activities, including the holding of any public meeting, shouting of slogans, making speeches, picketing or dharnas, assembly of five or more persons, carrying fire arms, banners, placards, lathis, spears, swords, sticks, brickbats, etc.

The affidavit from the police chief came in response to a host of petitions filed by politicians, party leaders, activists, lawyers and private individuals — including CPI(M) state secretary M.A. Baby, Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi and others — against the indiscriminate detentions of leaders, former Chief Ministers, students, youths, journalists, lawyers, and others by the Delhi Police, against the rule of law and democratic dissent on October 10-11 during protests seeking the resignation of the CEC.

The petitioners had alleged around 7,000 en masse illegal detentions during the protests, and shutting down of vital public transport systems, including the Delhi Metro, leaving thousands of commuters stranded in the national capital. Major roads had been heavily barricaded with the heavy presence of security personnel, and trains to Delhi were cancelled on October 10 amidst the detentions.

Mr. Tripathi, through his counsel Chand Qureshi, had argued in the apex court that the shutdown was in clear violation of an October 9 order of the Supreme Court, which had emphasised that the authorities must not cause any hardship or suffering to ordinary commuters through a blanket ban.
This had led the Supreme Court to direct the Delhi Police to place on record the specific prohibitive orders.

articles.title: Why is there variation in India’s fertility rates? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: What is the Total Fertility Rate of India? How does it impact policy interventions?

The story so far: The Sample Registration System (SRS) Statistical Report of 2021, released by the Office of the Registrar General of India recently, showed that India has maintained its Total Fertility Rate (TFR) at 2.0 — the same as reported in 2020. While the national average for TFR has remained the same, there is a wide regional variation in TFR data for States and Union Territories (UTs) reported independently.

The highest TFR was recorded in Bihar at 3.0 and the lowest was reported for West Bengal and Delhi at 1.4. The data went on to reveal that in the decade between 2009-11 and 2019-21, TFR has been on an overall decline, in States, and nationally, albeit at different rates.

articles.title: Row over Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free Deepavali | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BMC uploaded the videos on November 1, but soon after the video of actor Dia Mirza went up, BJP Mumbai president Ameet Satam is learnt to have called the BMC administration to pull it down

The story so far: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) expressed strong displeasure and asked the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to restore a video of actor Dia Mirza, in which, the actor appealed for a noise-free and pollution-free celebration of Deepavali. The message was a part of the official anti-firecracker campaign of the BMC. The civic body pulled down the video earlier this week after objections by the BJP leaders.

In a suo motu Public Interest Litigation about noise and air pollution caused by religious processions across Maharashtra, the Bombay High Court had urged to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) to rope in celebrities for pollution awareness.

articles.title: Vijayawada civic poll result: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna elected Mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jana Sena’s Vangaveeti Radhakrishna is elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes
The National Democratic Alliance of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) , the Jana Sena Party (JSP) and the BJP has won a landslide victory in Vijayawada in the urban local body elections.

Delayed by continuous rain, the counting process , which began at around 3 p.m. on Tuesday, continued till late night. Election personnel worked till around 4 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026). The final results were announced by the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation on Wednesday morning.
The city has 8,05,797 voters across 86 divisions, of whom 4,46,021 exercised their franchise on Sunday (November 1). Of these, 4,27,385 votes were declared valid.

విజయవాడ మున్సిపల్ కార్పొరేషన్ మేయర్ గా కూటమి బలపరచిన జనసేన పార్టీ అభ్యర్థి శ్రీ వంగవీటి రాధాకృష్ణ గారు భారీ మెజారిటీతో ఘన విజయం సాధించిన సందర్భంగా శుభాకాంక్షలు. #NDAsweepsAP #APLocalBodyElections #JanaSenaStrikesAgain #CheppaamChestunnaam https://t.co/lY6g9acvuy

According to the final report on votes secured by each Mayoral candidate, JSP candidate Vangaveeti Radhakrishna got 2,65,968 votes. YSRCP candidate and former Mayor Rayana Bhagyalakshmi came second with 1,35,056 votes.

Independent candidate and former Vijayawada Police Commissioner A.B. Venkateswara Rao, who was supported by the Congress and the CPI and the CPI(M), secured 12,657 votes. His entry had made it a three-way contest, but Mr. Venkateswara Rao could not save his deposit: he failed to secure one-sixth of the total number of votes polled.

Vangaveeti Radhakrishna, with TDP leaders Buddha Venkanna and Gadde Anuradha, at a rally in Vijayawada on October 18, before filing his nomination for the Mayor’s post. He was elected Mayor by a margin of 1,30,912 votes. File | Photo Credit: G.N. Rao
Aam Aadmi Party candidate Kambhampati Rama Gopala Krishna Murthy got 499 votes. There were 19 candidates in the fray for the Mayor’s post, ten of them independents.

The TDP and its alliance partners also swept the division elections. The TDP won 53 divisions, the Jana Sena Party 19 and the BJP four. In total, the alliance won 76 of the 86 divisions of the Vijayawada Municipal Corporation.

The YSRCP, which won the municipal elections in Vijayawada in 2021, was reduced to eight divisions. The CPI(M)’s candidate, former corporator Boye Satya Babu, held his division, and an independent candidate won another.

The divisions the YSRCP won are 34, 53 and 58 in the Vijayawada West Assembly constituency, 78 in Vijayawada Central, and 6, 8, 10 and 26 in Vijayawada East. Mr. Satya Babu won Division 52 in the West constituency.

The TDP won the most divisions, 20, in the Vijayawada Central constituency, and 17 and 16 in the East and West constituencies respectively. The JSP won seven divisions each in the East and West constituencies and five in Central. The BJP won one division each in West and East and two in Central.

articles.title: Rescue operation at landslide-hit south Odisha village halted; families prepare for final rituals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision to temporarily suspend the operation was taken after experts assessed that the remains, if any, could be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris, Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said

The multi-agency search and rescue operation at landslide-ravaged Gidipabali village in south Odisha was halted on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) due to inclement weather, as families of 10 missing persons prepared to perform their final rituals, a senior official said.

The decision to temporarily suspend the operation was taken after experts assessed that the remains, if any, could be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris, Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said.
He, along with Ganjam District Collector V Keerthi Vasan, met the victims’ family members at a shelter camp and discussed the situation at the site where the search and rescue operation was underway.
The State Government had launched the search and rescue operation on Friday (October 30, 2026) following the landslide triggered by heavy rains brought by Cyclone Arnab last week.

“According to experts, there is at least 30 feet of debris, which is difficult to remove due to at least three successive landslides in the area. Further blasting is likely to trigger fresh landslides and may also endanger the lives of rescue personnel. Therefore, with the consent of the family members, the rescue operation was halted on Wednesday,” Kandhamal Collector Vedbhusan told reporters.
He said the families, understanding the difficult circumstances and challenges involved, had requested the administration to help them perform the final rituals and find closure.

“The administration has assured the families of all possible assistance to help them restart their lives. However, we want to make one more final attempt to ensure closure for everyone,” the collector said.

“Although operations have been temporarily halted on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) due to the weather, we will make another round of efforts as soon as the weather remains clear for a couple of days before closing the operation, as per the wishes of the families,” he added.

The official said the State Government had mobilised multiple agencies and deployed all possible resources, including life-detection equipment, dog squads, experts from IIT, the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Railway teams and controlled blasting, for the rescue operation.
However, no significant breakthrough was achieved, as the houses affected by the landslide are believed to be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris following successive landslides.
Of the 26 residents of Gidipabali, a hilltop village on the Kandhamal-Ganjam district border, 13 managed to escape the landslide on the night of October 29 and were shifted to a shelter in Udayagiri.
The search operation was launched for the remaining 13 residents.

articles.title: ECI still insisting on Form 6 for excluded voters in Delhi SIR, petitioners make urgent mentioning in Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: On October 28, the Supreme Court made it clear that the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), said that the Election Commission of India (ECI) was still insisting that voters excluded after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Delhi, under the Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate (ASDD) categories, must fill up Form 6, meant exclusively for new voters. fill up Form 6, which is meant exclusively for new voters.

On October 28, the Supreme Court made it clear that the ECI was in “error” to force pre-existing voters, deleted from the electoral rolls, to apply as new voters under Form 6 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.

Petitioners, activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, represented by advocates Mr. Bhushan, Cheryl D’souza and Neha Rathi, had submitted on October 28 that the ECI was compelling voters to misrepresent themselves as new applicants, an offence which attracts imprisonment.
On October 28, the apex court had orally nudged the ECI that such purged voters should be allowed to use Form 8/enumeration form.
On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the CJI said the case would be heard after Deepavali holidays, the voters need not fear when the Supreme Court was already dealing with the case.
The CJI noted that the ECI has extended the deadline for filing claims and objections to November 25 from the earlier deadline of October 30.
Mr. Bhushan said the voters feared that making a declaration in Form 6 that they were fresh voters would invite prosecution.
“They are in the horns of a dilemma,” Mr. Bhushan submitted.
“We are dealing with the matter, how can they feel like that,” the CJI assured.
The Bench asked the petitioners to file an application on this aspect, and said the matter would be heard on November 19.
Editorial | Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
If required, the Bench further stated that the ECI could be asked to extend the date further.

articles.title: Union Cabinet to discuss capex support for critical mineral processing, VGF for RE grid-scale storage system
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants

The Union Cabinet is expected to take up two major schemes for consideration, the first of them concerns according capital expenditure support for promoting critical mineral processing and the other being a viability gap funding (VGF) scheme for development of grid-scale storage system, according to a memo seen by The Hindu.
The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).
Although the memo did not specify the contours of the scheme and its ambit, the policy has been in the works for some time now.
The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants.

At an event of the industry body FIMI in September this year, Secretary at the Union Ministry of Mines Keshav Chandra had indicated that the government would institute a scheme for domestic processing of lithium and nickel.

Back in April, the Piyush Goyal, the former secretary, had indicated that the government had identified two minerals for initiating the scheme that were, among other things, expected to provide resilience the electric vehicle battery chain.

Grid-scale energy storage systems are deployed at transmission and distribution for greater grid stability, absorb excess electricity when supply exceeds demand and discharge them during peak hours or when necessary.

About 1,835 million units (MUs) of renewable energy was curtailed, according to data compiled by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) during July and August this year. This includes 1,462 MU of solar energy and 373 MU of wind energy.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries is already implementing a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for establishing 50 GWh of advanced chemistry cell manufacturing capacity, of which 10 GWh would account for grid-scale stationary storage.

articles.title: Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty after Trump’s Republicans face election rout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran

Oil prices rose on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) in a volatile session as investors ​awaited Washington’s next move in the war with Iran, with ⁠Democrats capturing control of US Congress from President Donald Trump’s Republicans in midterm elections.
Brent futures rose 82 cents, or 0.8%, to $104.42 a barrel at 0510 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude ‌futures gained 50 cents, or 0.5%, to $96.59, reversing earlier declines.
In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
Vote ‌counting ⁠was underway in the U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats snaring majorities ⁠in both houses of Congress for the rest of Trump’s second term.

“President Trump’s conflicting signals, with military strikes continuing alongside statements downplaying further escalation, have made it difficult for traders to build strong directional ​conviction,” said Priyanka Sachdeva, head ‌of market insights at Phillip Nova.
“I believe some profit-taking and reduction in speculative long positions are justified, particularly after the sharp rally in October,” said Sachdeva.

“However, the underlying supply disruption risks around the Strait of Hormuz have not disappeared. ‌An unexpected drawdown in U.S. crude inventories is also offering some fundamental ​support,” she added.

The U.S. had carried out “defensive” strikes on Iran’s Qeshm island targeting surface-to-air missiles used against US assets, a US official said ⁠on Tuesday. Another official said the strikes appeared limited and did not signal a return to major combat operations.
Markets remained on watch for any progress in talks ‌to end the US-Israeli war with Iran, as Qatar stepped up mediation efforts to avert an escalation of attacks after the US elections.
A senior Iranian official told Reuters on Tuesday that Iran and the United States remain far from a deal to end their war.
U.S. President Donald Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran.
Meanwhile, crude ‌stocks fell by 5.27 million barrels in the week ended October 30, market sources said on ​Wednesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.

articles.title: NMDC’s iron ore output rose 18% in Oct, sales dip amid rain impact

fullParagraphs: Dispatches were temporarily impacted by disruptions to the Kottavalasa–Kirandul (KK) railway line after sections of the route were washed away due to heavy monsoon rains in September and October.
State-owned NMDC reported October iron ore production rose 18% year-on-year (YoY) to 5.04 million tonnes, while sales declined more than 11% to 3.44 MT.

“The 18% growth in iron ore production in October reflects the sustained efforts of the teams. articles.title: Petronet LNG reports 52.3% growth in net profits, in talks for availing undelivered cargoes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Along with their results, Petronet LNG also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share

State-owned Petronet LNG reported 53.2% growth in net profits in the September-end quarter, driven by improved operational efficiency, although cargoes from its most prominent supplier, Qatar, continued to be affected because of the reignited conflict in West Asia.
The company also declared a dividend of ₹7 per equity share.
The country’s largest LNG importer’s net profit stood at ₹1,235 crore in the reported quarter against ₹806 crore in the same period last year.
Revenue from operations although declined about 35% during the period to ₹7,200.35 crore.
The company processed 231 trillion British Thermal Units (TBTU) during the period, higher than 228 TBTU it processed in the same period last year.
Overall capacity utilisation in the reported quarter narrowed to 64% against 78% in the same period last year.
Capacity utilisation at their Dahej terminal stood at 73% against 92% in the comparable period last year.

Speaking to the press, Akshay Kumar Singh, Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) informed that the company was also in talks with QatarEnergy to secure delivery of the cargoes that could not be delivered because of the force majeure.
“On the sidelines, we also discuss if they would be able to give more cargoes before the contractual date. If there is a requirement in the country, we will take that as well,” he said.
The supplier has declared forced majeure until December-end.
Mr. Singh told reporters that the contractual terms have provisions to recoup the lost cargoes for one year after the expiry of the current contract period, that is, May 2028.
He stated that Petronet LNG lost an average 9-10 cargoes each month in the last eight months, thus, about 75-80 cargoes whilst it has received 6 cargoes from the supplier.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

Mr. Gohil invoked an assurance given by the then Finance Minister Jaswant Singh in Parliament in August 2003 that the government’s stake in IDBI Bank would not be reduced below 51%. A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had also favoured retaining the government’s majority stake, he said.

He further questioned the regulatory concessions extended to Fairfax, including the two-year window reportedly allowed to reduce its control in another Indian bank, and sought details of the source of funds for the acquisition.

articles.title: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed claims victory in Michigan Senate battle
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed said early on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that he had won a US Senate seat in Michigan over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, which would make him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress.
“Michigan, we did it!” Mr. El-Sayed said in a speech at his election headquarters in Detroit.
“I am so proud and honored to stand here as your senator-elect from the great state of Michigan.”
Mr. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute hiccup in his campaign when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers at the 11th hour.
The Michigan doctor rallied voters on leftist campaign promises, including universal health care, to hold a key U.S. Senate seat for Democrats, taking over from the retiring Gary Peters.
Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded Mr. El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.
But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s thorny health care system.
“You deserve to be able to see a doctor without getting a huge bill,” he told Michiganders on the eve of the vote, vowing to upend America’s divisive multi-billion-dollar for-profit medical system.
During the race, Mr. El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
Mr. El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.
The election makes Mr. El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969.

articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries poised to become first Black Speaker of U.S. House of Representatives
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: As Speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York ​City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years

The Democrats’ midterm election win puts Hakeem Jeffries in line to become the first Black speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, with the dual challenge of opposing President ‌Donald Trump while bridging the gap between his party’s moderates and its more vocal progressives.

As Speaker, Mr. Jeffries, representing a New York ​City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans ⁠who controlled the House for the past four years.
“Today begins the great American comeback,” Mr. Jeffries proclaimed in a victory speech late on Tuesday after media outlets projected the likelihood of Democratic majorities in the House and Senate.

He attacked the Trump-led Republican agenda in Congress over the past two years, pledging to pass legislation reversing steep spending cuts — enacted into ‌law on July 4, 2025 — to the Medicaid healthcare program for the poor and people with disabilities.

“The American people have spoken and made clear that they’ve had enough of the extremism, enough of the corruption. They want a Congress that’s going to deliver for the ‌American people,” Mr. Jeffries said.

He has stopped short of saying the House, under his leadership, would attempt to impeach Trump for a third time.

articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: List of Indian-origin winners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

Several Indian-origin candidates too notched up victories as Democrats made significant gains in the US midterm elections, positioning themselves to wrest key Senate seats from Republicans, delivering a stinging rebuke to President Donald Trump.

Indian-American candidates Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives from Virginia and Florida, respectively. On the other hand, Republican ‌Vivek ‌Ramaswamy ‌was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor.

Suhas Subramanyam, who served as an advisor to former president Barack Obama, has been re-elected as a member of the US House of Representatives. The 40-year-old won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district , polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4 per cent of the ballots cast.

A former high school principal, Pia Dandiya became the newest Indian-American to be elected to the US House , defeating Republican Casey Askar in Florida’s 22nd Congressional district. Dandiya bagged 51.9% of the votes, while her opponent Askar polled 49.1% of the votes.

Trump favourite Indian-American Vivek Ramaswamy was defeated in Ohio’s gubernatorial race, the home state of Vice President J. D. Vance, by Democrat Amy Acton after a bitter campaign that left the Republican Party divided.

Other Indian-American candidates are awaiting their results as vote counting is still under way. Democrat Nithya Raman, who was born in Keralam, is locked in a keen contest with her former boss Karen Bass for the post of Mayor of Los Angeles, the US’s second-largest city. Indian-American lawmakers Ro Khanna, Ami Bera, Pramila Jayapal are seeking re-election to the US House of Representatives, while fellow Democrat Amish Shah is in the fray in competitive races to make their debut as Congresspersons.

fullParagraphs: The research found that producing green hydrogen in desert areas in Australia, Chile and north Africa needs far more water than the industry claims. It also found serious environmental risks that had been overlooked

Green hydrogen is a form of renewable energy that, if taken up widely, could reduce global greenhouse gas emissions. It is produced by splitting water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen using renewable power. This clean, zero-emissions fuel is mainly used by industries like steel manufacturing and chemical refining. Heavy transport sectors such as maritime shipping, aviation and long-haul trucking could also use it.

But green hydrogen comes at an environmental cost too: huge amounts of water are needed to produce it. In Africa, the regions that have the best solar and wind resources to produce this clean energy are also those with the least water on the planet.

articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

There have always been stories about them. Australian Aboriginal tales tell of an old couple called the Jukara, while for Chile’s Mapuche people they are Rvganko or water ponds. To modern astronomers, they are the Small and Large Magellanic clouds, two of the closest galaxies to us that are in the process of being swallowed by the Milky Way.

They are evidence of a kind of snowball effect that characterises the formation and evolution of galaxies, which scientists believe are the result of a series of violent collisions. As galaxies fall into one another, the smaller ones are ripped apart by tidal forces of the larger, leaving behind streams and clusters of stars that don’t move in lockstep with the rest of the galaxy. They also stand out for their chemical compositions, which allow astronomers to group stars that were born together and piece back their rough ages.

Science, Space & Environment Report: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports

Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

There have always been stories about them. Australian Aboriginal tales tell of an old couple called the Jukara, while for Chile’s Mapuche people they are Rvganko or water ponds. To modern astronomers, they are the Small and Large Magellanic clouds, two of the closest galaxies to us that are in the process of being swallowed by the Milky Way.

They are evidence of a kind of snowball effect that characterises the formation and evolution of galaxies, which scientists believe are the result of a series of violent collisions. As galaxies fall into one another, the smaller ones are ripped apart by tidal forces of the larger, leaving behind streams and clusters of stars that don’t move in lockstep with the rest of the galaxy. They also stand out for their chemical compositions, which allow astronomers to group stars that were born together and piece back their rough ages.

articles.title: Many parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 379 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on November 4, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

The overall air quality of Delhi continued to be in the “very poor” category on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) morning, while many parts of the city reeled under “severe” level of air pollution , according to official data.
Many parts of the city, including ITO, Dwarka, Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, Alipur, Bawana, and Jahangirpuri witnessed “severe” level air pollution.
Other cities and towns in north India, including Noida, Gurugram, and Panipat also witnessed “very poor” air quality, on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) morning.
The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 379 (very poor) at 9 a.m. on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data.
“Severe” level air pollution affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, as per the CPCB.
The overall air quality of Delhi is likely to be in the “very poor” category for three days, as per the Central government’s ‘Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi’.

The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi stood at 350 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on Tuesday, up from 324 (very poor) a day earlier, as per the Central Pollution Control Board’s daily bulletin, which is treated as the day’s AQI.

Every winter, air pollution spikes in Delhi-NCR and many parts of the larger Indo-Gangetic Plains, mainly due to meteorological factors such as lower wind speeds and a drop in temperature. Also, pollution from stubble burning during October and November and bursting of firecrackers during the festive season add to existing pollution from vehicles and dust, worsening the air quality.

articles.title: Cancer registry in Telangana has logged 35,000 cases, government advisor informs Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Minister for Health C. Damodar Raja Narasimha says Telangana government has expanded cancer treatment services to all 33 districts in the State

The Telangana government has expanded cancer treatment services to all 33 districts in the State, with day-care cancer centres providing chemotherapy locally to reduce the need for patients to travel to Hyderabad, Minister for Health C. Damodar Raja Narasimha said on Tuesday, November 3. The government has also initiated steps to establish Regional Cancer Centres to further strengthen cancer care infrastructure, he added.
The Minister made these remarks during a review meeting on medical services being provided to cancer patients in government hospitals.

Oncologist Dr. Nori Dattatreyudu, who also serves as the advisor to the Telangana government on preventive, curative and affordable cancer care, said 35,000 cancer cases have been registered on the dedicated cancer portal. “Declaring cancer a notifiable disease and effective use of cancer registry will help strengthen the State’s efforts in monitoring and controlling the disease,” he added.

Citing the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination programme as an example, Dr. Nori also appreciated the State’s efforts in prevention, screening and early detection of cancer. Of the 3.4 lakh eligible girls in Telangana, 2.3 lakh of them have been vaccinated against the HPV, achieving a coverage of 67%, he said.

During the meeting, officials briefed the Minister on cancer treatment facilities available at the MNJ Cancer Hospital and the Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), besides the functioning of day-care chemotherapy centres established across the State. They explained that while patients initially receive treatment at MNJ or NIMS, chemotherapy services are subsequently provided at district-level centres. Patients are also being mapped district-wise to facilitate treatment and follow-up.

The Minister directed officials to improve facilities for patients receiving chemotherapy at district centres and ensure that the services were readily available at the district headquarters. “Patients should not have to travel to Hyderabad for chemotherapy when treatment could be provided closer to their homes,” he added.

articles.title: IndiaAI Mission releases indigenous foundation models EKA-1, Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: These three indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating homegrown AI technology

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY), on Tuesday released indigenous foundation models EKA-1, developed by Soket Labs Technology and Research, and Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, developed by ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations, marking another step in the country's push to build homegrown AI capabilities.
The models were unveiled at an event attended by IT Secretary S Krishnan, senior officials from the ministry and IndiaAI, as well as the leadership of both companies.
These three indigenous models are a key milestone under the IndiaAI Mission, showcasing India's progress in creating homegrown AI technology.

Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B enable offline-capable, document-grounded automation, knowledge retrieval and citizen or enterprise services across defence, government, industrial and educational sectors, particularly in low-connectivity or sensitive environments.
Both firms are among the teams selected under the IndiaAI Innovation Centre (Foundation Models) pillar, which aims to build indigenous AI capabilities and large language models.

The government said access to subsidised national AI compute infrastructure, along with support for ancillary research expenses, enabled the development of the models. It cited this as an example of how public AI infrastructure can speed up homegrown innovation.

Built for Indian languages, banking and cybersecurity, the EKA-1 has 26.3 billion parameters and was trained on about 7.5 trillion tokens. It covers all 22 scheduled Indian languages along with English. Soket describes it as an open, sparse hybrid language model designed for math, code, reasoning and agentic use.
EKA-1 can be used even without a mobile data or WiFi connection, as it has the capability to do certain inferencing on the local device, say a smartphone.

Soket CEO Abhishek Upperwal said the model has been tailored to India's banking, financial services and cybersecurity landscape. It is meant to address sector-specific requirements and understand the country's evolving digital ecosystem, he said.
ZenteiQ's Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B are open-source models that support English and 10 Indian languages. They can be deployed as secure, on-premise multilingual assistants.
According to an official release, the focus is on low-connectivity or sensitive environments.

ZenteiQ CEO Prof. Sashikumar said the models can run on different computing platforms, including GPUs and TPUs. Their lightweight architecture also allows on-device deployment on mobile phones without depending on cloud connectivity, he said.

articles.title: Business, unusual: On engaging with the Myanmar junta
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Engaging with the Myanmar junta is a short-sighted move

Months after a sham election that installed junta chief Min Aung Hlaing as Myanmar’s civilian President, the military continues to wage war on its own people even as the world has largely looked away. More than a lakh people are estimated to have died since the 2021 coup, many in fighting between the junta and the anti-coup People’s Defence Forces and ethnic armed organisations. The junta has also killed thousands of civilians in air strikes on villages in rebel-held areas to terrorise communities into giving up their resistance. With wars affecting Ukraine, Gaza, Sudan and Yemen, and Iran, the world has grown numb to such violence. The junta has exploited that indifference and a shifting geopolitical situation to act with impunity. Russia and China, its principal arms suppliers, have stood by it with the former supplying jets that were used to bomb civilians. Beijing, which tacitly allowed three ethnic armed organisations to launch an offensive in Shan and Rakhine States in late 2023, has since pressured two of them into ceasefires and returning seized territory. It also backed the January election. Since being sworn in, Min Aung Hlaing has visited India , Thailand, Vietnam and three other ASEAN member-states. ASEAN still swears by its Five-Point Consensus, which calls for an end to violence and dialogue. Yet, its members seem more than eager to do business with a regime that has flouted every point. Meanwhile, U.S. officials reportedly held secret talks with the junta in Tokyo in June and October, and a senior delegation met Min Aung Hlaing in Naypyidaw in September. Japan is reportedly pressing the Financial Action Task Force to take Myanmar off its blacklist.

The motives are not hard to understand. China wants an outlet to the Indian Ocean and security for its oil and gas pipelines. It has also played both sides, dealing with the junta and powerful rebel groups such as the Kachin Independence Organisation, whose territory is rich in rare earths and jade, and the United Wa State Army, which runs a massive tin mine. New Delhi wants to revive its stalled Act East policy, including the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project. The U.S. eyes access to mining vital heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium, for use in electric vehicles and weapons systems. What these short-sighted overtures miss is that trade thrives in a country at peace, not one where armed groups are perennially battling for control. The junta which has killed its citizens and has scuttled every move towards democracy cannot deliver that peace. Unless the generals are made to answer for their war crimes, Myanmar will remain a war zone. It will be ruinous not only for its hapless people but also for businesses seeking to trade with it.

articles.title: Coming of age: On the Binance hack
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Binance’s reaction to the hack shows how the crypto industry has matured

The recent hack at Binance, the biggest theft ever at the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, has lessons for India. But Indian policymakers must be careful to learn the right ones. First, it must be understood that the hack is not an indictment of the crypto space itself. Being a crypto exchange did not make Binance more vulnerable than if it were, say, a bank. Hacking is now a daily occurrence across sectors and even small pharmaceutical companies often have to fend off millions of attacks a month. Of course, Binance must look into how it was hacked and prevent a recurrence, but the cat-and-mouse game between hackers and security software developers is a perpetual one. For every million, or even billion, attacks that are stopped, one will inevitably get through. The lesson for Indian policymakers is not that crypto is unsafe in itself; this incident does not prove that. Rather, it is about how Binance prepared for and reacted to the attack. Back in 2018, Binance had set up an emergency fund called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to protect user assets in the event of a security breach or platform-level incident. The fund was created for exactly this kind of incident, and was financed through trading fees that Binance collects from users. Since the $6.3 billion worth of assets stolen exceeded the SAFU’s resources, Binance dipped into its own resources to restore about 95% of users’ assets within four days of the hack.

So, Binance used a stable source of revenue to finance an emergency fund, which it deployed when an emergency occurred. The system worked perfectly, also showing how maturely and responsibly the crypto space can be run. The Indian government and the Reserve Bank of India still view the private crypto space as the Wild West of techno-finance. This is no longer the case. Large crypto companies are employing prudential practices, safeguarding customers, and cooperating with law enforcement agencies. If the fear is that cryptocurrencies are not backed by any asset, then Indian policymakers can choose to allow only stablecoins, which do have real assets underpinning them. Indians are not at higher risk from cryptos than they are from fake stock market scams. The best defence is awareness. By refusing to regulate the crypto space in India and, indeed, taxing it at a prohibitive rate, the government is driving Indians towards either the black market, where such scams proliferate, or foreign exchanges. The government can take a leaf out of Binance’s book and mandate an industry-maintained emergency fund. There is ample international legislation to emulate now. The point is, crypto risks have fallen and adoption is rising. Now is the time to regulate the industry.

articles.title: DVAC conducts drone survey of irrigation tank in illegal sand mining charge against DMK’s E.V. Velu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted a drone survey of an irrigation tank in Malappambadi village near Tiruvannamalai in connection with allegations of illegal sand mining by former PWD and Highways Minister and senior DMK leader E.V. Velu for the party’s Northern Zone Youth Wing Conference held on December 14, 2025.

DVAC sources said that the drone survey was conducted in coordination with the Revenue Department, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, and the police to assess the extent of damage done to the water body. It will also provide total depth and width of the tank that was mined for the purpose. by illegal sand mining. The survey was monitored by Ganesan, Deputy SP, DVAC (Ranipet), K.Selvam, Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO), Tiruvannamalai, and K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner.

The assessment comes in the wake of a complaint filed by Arappor Iyakkam , an NGO, with the DVAC at its headquarters in Chennai on August 13 this year. The complaint alleged that large volumes of sand was illegally mined from the irrigation tank reportedly based on directions by the then PWD and Highways Minister Mr. Velu. The sand theft has reportedly incurred a loss to a tune of ₹8 crore to State exchequer, the complainant claimed.

The sand was mined to reportedly level an open land of 124.56 acres, to organise the DMK’s conference. The conference was attended by former Chief Minister and DMK president M.K. Stalin and his son and former Deputy Chief Minister Udhayanidhi Stalin.

The complaint also alleged that Mr. Velu, who was appointed as DMK’s northern zonal in-charge for 2026 Assembly polls, for personally overseeing and directing the logistical arrangements for the conference. “The sand from the tank bed was illegally mined to a depth of around 10 feet to 23 feet to an extent around 12 acres as against the permissible limit of one metre in depth under Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1959. The excavated sand can be used only for local agricultural, pottery and domestic purposes,” the complaint said.

articles.title: Probe launched into derailment of goods wagons at Jolarpet Railway Station
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Southern Railway has ordered an inquiry into the derailment of seven goods wagons at a yard near Jolarpet Railway Station in Tirupattur.
Railway officials said that seven wagons got derailed for around 400 metres, when the train was being moved from a loop line to the main line in the yard near the railway station.

Railway officials said that no untoward incident happened as the route towards Bengaluru, where the derailment occurred, had less traffic movement. The incident occurred around 7.15 p.m. on November 1.

Railway officials said that the Bengaluru SBC to Jolarpet JTJ MEMU train was short-terminated at Somanayakkanpti Railway Station in Tirupattur. Senior officials and engineering crews from the Salem and Chennai railway divisions immediately rushed to the spot to restore train services, which resumed around 12.30 a.m. on November 1.
This is the second incident after five wagons of an empty goods train, coming from Chennai port, derailed at Kethandapatti village near Jolarpet Railway Station in November, 2024.

articles.title: Rajanna is free to quit party if he wishes: Balakrishna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Congress leader and Minister for Municipal Administration H.C. Balakrishna lashed out at senior Congress leader and MLA K.N. Rajanna on Tuesday, saying he was free to quit the party if he so wished, and accusing him of “betraying the party while being part of it.”
This comes against the backdrop of Mr. Rajanna’s son and MLC R. Rajendra recently meeting JD(S) leader and Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy.

Speaking to reporters in Chitradurga, he said, “If Mr. Rajanna wants to leave the party and join another party, he is free to do so. Let him honestly answer whether his son contested the election fairly. The election process had not even concluded when he posed for a photograph with Mr. Kumaraswamy. If the Congress party does not pay attention to such issues, it may have to face serious problems in the future. Mr. Rajanna is betraying the party while remaining in it. The party does not belong to any one individual. He has engaged in anti-party activities, and strict action should be taken against him. We will lodge a complaint against Mr. Rajanna with the party high command.”

articles.title: Bengaluru: South corporation shuts 63 commercial establishments in residential layouts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bengaluru South City Corporation has sealed 63 commercial establishments operating “illegally” in residential areas across its jurisdiction during a special enforcement drive conducted by officials.

The Corporation sealed the highest number of establishments in the BTM Layout Assembly constituency, where 30 shops were shut. This was followed by 10 in the Bengaluru South constituency, nine in Bommanahalli, eight in Padmanabhanagar, four in Jayanagar, and two within the limits of the Anekal Assembly constituency (part of which falls under the South City Corporation).

According to Corporation officials, the action targeted commercial establishments operating in residential areas in violation of regulations. Officials said they were causing inconvenience to residents and obstructing vehicular movement. Bakeries, eateries, condiment stores, salons, beauty parlours, fruit and vegetable outlets, hardware stores, and other commercial establishments were among those sealed.

The Corporation said commercial establishments operating on roads narrower than 40 feet in residential areas were prohibited. However, several establishments had continued operations without valid trade licences despite being issued notices and instructions to vacate.

The drive was conducted simultaneously across several wards in Kumaraswamy Layout, J.P. Nagar, Madiwala, Koramangala, Ejipura, Jakkasandra, Begur, Singasandra, Yelachenahalli, Uttarahalli, Gottigere, Bilekahalli and Arakere, among others.
Commissioner K.N. Ramesh warned of strict legal action against establishments operating illegally or without the necessary licences.

articles.title: CMC organises Graduation Day for Super Specialty and Fellowship Postgraduates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Christian Medical College (CMC) has organised a graduation day for Super Speciality and Fellowship Postgraduates at its campus in Vellore.

According to a press release, Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Tamil Nadu Department of Health and Family Welfare Department, was the chief guest. In his address, Mr. Ahamed highlighted CMC’s long-standing commitment to serving underserved communities. He also emphasised challenges faced by graduates, including an ageing population, the rise in non-communicable diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and climate change related health challenges. The official also highlighted the growing role of artificial intelligence in healthcare.

A total of 189 postgraduates were presented certificates by the college principal, Solomon Sathishkumar, in the presence of Vaibhav Londhe, Associate Director, CMC, and I. Rajesh, Medical Superintendent, CMC, the release said.

articles.title: Trump says U.S. cutting $3.8 billion annual security assistance to Israel
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Washington is ending a 10-year security assistance accord with Israel that allowed $3.8 billion in annual assistance to its ally until 2028.
Mr. Trump said Israel was “fine” with him ending the assistance, which began in 2019 and was signed under his predecessor, Barack Obama, three years earlier.
“We’ll help Israel if they need it,” Mr. Trump added in an interview on “Fox and Friends,” saying that he had agreed with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cut the assistance.
“Israel’s our number one; we give them more than anybody else, and they no longer need it... If they did need it, I would say keep it going,” Mr. Trump added.
Under the deal, Israel receives financial assistance for the purchase of around $3.8 billion in weapons a year.

Since its founding in 1948, Israel has received more than $300 billion, adjusted for inflation, in U.S. economic and military assistance, according to the Council on Foreign Relations, far more than any other country since 1946.
The Israeli premier has said he wanted to end Israel’s reliance on U.S. support.
In June, Mr. Netanyahu called for his country to increase its military autonomy and reduce its reliance on Washington.
In January, he told The Economist that he hoped to do so within a decade, while in May he told CBS that he wanted support to reach “zero”.
Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) announcement was nonetheless met with backlash from Israeli opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot, who said it showed that Mr. Netanyahu must go.

“The fact that Israel’s defense establishment is learning of a shift in our strategic relationship through the media, at the same time as the Israeli public, shows just how dangerous Benjamin Netanyahu’s conduct is,” Mr. Eisenkot said in a statement.

On Tuesday (November 3, 2026), Mr. Trump cited attacks by leftist Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the U.S. Senate in Tuesday’s (November 3, 2026) midterm elections after harnessing popular discontent and anti-Israel sentiment, as part of the reasoning behind the decision to end aid.
