articles.title: CM wants officials to hold regular discussions with Maha govt. on Tummidihatti barrage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Govt prepared to keep compensation for submergence areas in joint account, he said

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed the Irrigation department officials to hold negotiations with the neighbouring Maharashtra government on increasing the height of Tummidihatti barrage on a regular basis.

Officials have been directed to be prepared with information pertaining to area that will come under submergence and other details. Steps should be taken to submit information and documents relating to agreements entered into between the two States in the past. The Chief Minister gave the directions during a meeting with senior officials to review the progress achieved in the irrigation projects on Tuesday. The meeting follows the Chief Minister’s recent meeting with his Maharashtra counterpart Devendra Fadnavis in Mumbai where the two States discussed about raising the height of Tummidihatti barrage to 152 metres enabling flow of water through gravity to backward districts like Adilabad.

He reiterated the Telangana government’s preparedness to pay appropriate compensation to Maharashtra for the lands that would be submerged if the height of the Tummidihatti barrage was increased to 152 metres. Steps would be taken to ensure that the required funds would be kept in joint account. He reiterated that the Telangana government would not object to any survey that would be conducted by Maharashtra to assess the areas that would be subject to submergence and wanted the Irrigation department officials to be prepared with the information sought by the neighbouring State in this regard.

articles.title: Regularisation of Section 22A lands in Telangana trudges slowly
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rectification of lapses that occurred in the declaration of lands under Section 22A of the Registration Act and their regularisation in Telangana is moving at a snail’s pace.

The process reportedly slowed down as some district collectors are learnt to have submitted the lists of Section 22A lands under their purview in pdf format and the same have been uploaded on Registration and Stamps website. Since scanned documents with village as unit have been uploaded on the website, changes/corrections in the date can be made only after reopening the entire document.

Given the workload on the Revenue staff and technical problems in the website which are not infrequent, effecting changes/corrections is taking time putting the owners to difficulties, thereby resulting in delays in the transactions. The development follows the furore raised by people over thousands of genuine private properties , residential plots, and older homes across Hyderabad and surrounding districts like Rangareddy, Medchal, and Sangareddy being mistakenly flagged and placed on the prohibited list due to clerical errors, technical issues, and legacy data issues from earlier portal transitions.

While the Opposition parties — the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) in particular — alleged that huge tracts of land had been placed under the prohibited list, the government claimed that 3.73 lakh acres lands were in prohibited list currently as the government had taken steps to regularise over 4 lakh acres in the past couple of years.

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has announced constitution of a high-level official committee to study the issue in-depth and suggest remedial measures so that not a single genuine land owner is adversely affected with one month deadline for submission of its recommendations. The committee, according to one of its members, has made several recommendations based on which the Revenue department had issued certain circulars/memos in the recent days. These included orders like G.O. 59 for speedy clearance of pending applications including those pertaining to the Urban Land Ceiling Act.

Legal experts are however finding fault with the process adopted claiming that the government or the committee have not shown any way out for regularising genuine lands declared as prohibited under Section 22A. “The recent circulars and memos deal with disposal of pending applications. There are no specific guidelines issued relating to lands erroneously placed under prohibited list,” a land laws expert said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: During the Dasara procession on October 21, the elephant carrying the howdah with the idol of Chamundeshwari suddenly turned back on the procession path and ran helter-skelter

A series of curative rituals, organised by the Shivamogga City Corporation following the untoward incident during the Dasara celebrations, began on November 3. Priests started the rituals at the Kote Seetharamanjaneya Swamy temple and the Kote Chandika Durgaparameshwari temple in Shivamogga.

During the Dasara procession on October 21, the elephant carrying the howdah with the idol of Chamundeshwari suddenly turned back on the procession path and ran helter-skelter. A portion of the howdah and a few vehicles were damaged in the melee. No casualties were reported.
Soon after the incident, priests and elected representatives of the city sought a ‘ religious remedy ’.

Shankarananda Jois, priest of the Kote Chandika Durgaparameshwari temple, told The Hindu on November 3 that, following request from people, the Deputy Commissioner wrote to the Endowment Department seeking suggestions.

“We met the seer of the Sringeri Mutt and sought his advice. I also consulted religious texts to find remedies so that such incidents do not recur. We prepared a list of rituals to be performed and also sought the opinion of the pundits of the Endowment Department,” he said.

On the advice of the experts, priests have begun homas and havanas at the two temples. On the first day, Mahasankalpa, Vishwaksena Puja and Navagraha Puja were held at the Kote Seetharamanjaneya temple. At the Kote Chandika Durgaparameshwari temple, the rituals included Mahaganapati Puja, Mahasankalpa, Punyahavachana, Ritvigvarana, Kushmanda Prayashchitta Homa, and Shannarikela Ashta Dravya Mahaganapati Homa.
“The homas and havanas will continue until November 7,” the priest said.
Shivamogga MLA S.N. Channabasappa, City Corporation Commissioner Mayanna Gowda and others took part in the mahasankalpa in the morning.

articles.title: T.N. govt. permits six shows a day for new Tamil films for a week from release date
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision was taken following representations from various film producers’ associations to the State government

The Tamil Nadu government on Tuesday announced that theatres across the State could now screen newly released Tamil films for up to six shows a day, from 6 a.m. to 2.30 a.m. the following day, for one week from the date of release.

According to an official release, based on the directions of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Cinemas (Regulation) Rules, 1957, would be amended suitably. The State government has also permitted six shows a day on local festival days, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays.

The decision was taken following representations from various film producers’ associations to the State government. After the TVK-led government assumed office, permission had been granted to screen newly released Tamil films for five shows a day for seven days from the date of release. Five shows a day were also permitted on local festival days, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays.

articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt operations at Warsaw airports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The bomb warnings targeted an SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen and a plane from London’s Heathrow airport operated by Polish airline LOT
Polish authorities said they received bomb threats Tuesday (November 3, 2026) involving two Warsaw-bound flights, but the planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
The bomb warnings targeted an SAS Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen and a plane from London's Heathrow airport operated by Polish airline LOT.
The Scandinavian Airlines plane landed at Warsaw's Chopin airport, where it underwent a security inspection that did not turn up any explosive devices.
The airport closed a landing strip, but was able to continue operating, an airport spokesman said.
The LOT flight, which had also been scheduled to arrive at Chopin, was diverted to the Polish capital's other airport, Warsaw Modlin.
"The passengers were evacuated and the plane underwent security checks. Nothing was found," airport spokesman Modlin Adam Szablowski told AFP .
"The airport has been reopened and is operating normally."
On Sunday (November 1), a bomb threat forced an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna to reroute to Bulgaria.

articles.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police, defy call to end protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Paramilitary forces have been deployed in Gazipur and Narayanganj as workers demanding a 30,000-taka minimum wage stay on the streets for a fourth day, with 58 police officers injured, the police said

Paramilitary forces were deployed in industrial suburbs around the Bangladesh capital as protests by garment sector workers demanding a wage hike stretched into their fourth day on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), defying calls to return to factories.

Protesters are still on the streets despite the government's announcement of a board to review the minimum wage in the vital garment industry, which employs millions of people and generates the bulk of Bangladesh's export earnings.
The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world's second-biggest garment exporter behind China, producing clothes for major international brands.

The police have filed cases against thousands of unidentified protesters for torching police vehicles and damaging property, with 58 officers injured since the protests began, police spokesperson Kamarum Munira said.
Workers said scores of protesters had also been injured, with demonstrators seen hurling bricks at the police, who in turn used batons and fired tear gas to disperse the crowds.

"Some factories are closed and workers have taken to the streets," Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Tuesday. "Some miscreants are trying to incite violence and make the situation more complicated."
The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh force said it had deployed forces in Gazipur and Narayanganj, key industrial suburbs around Dhaka, and was using drones to monitor the unrest.
The garment industry generates around four-fifths of Bangladesh's export earnings, worth up to $38 billion, and employs more than four million people.

Workers say the rising cost of food, housing, transport and healthcare has eroded their purchasing power in a country with 8% inflation. They are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, a 140% increase from the current 12,500 taka.
Industry representatives said on Monday (November 2, 2026) that workers from at least 670 factories had walked out.
Protesters in Gazipur blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway and set fire to roadside debris, but were later cleared by the police.
In Mirpur in Dhaka's northeast, a few hundred workers wielding sticks left their workplaces to join the protest, clashing with security forces.

articles.title: Kremlin confirms Ukraine-U.S. talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff earlier announced the meeting will take place on November 10-11
The Kremlin confirmed on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks to end more than four years of war will take place in Abu Dhabi next week.
U.S. President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff earlier announced the meeting will take place on November 10-11.

Mr. Witkoff met with both Russia's Vladimir Putin and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky last month, with all sides announcing three-way talks will resume in November, as Washington pushes an end to the dragging Ukraine-Russia war.
"The Russian delegation will arrive on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi to take part in trilateral talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters, including AFP .
The Russian delegation will be led by Putin aide Vladimir Medinsky, who took part in previous negotiations that failed to reach a breakthrough.

Mr. Medinsky, who was born in Ukraine, has co-authored Russian history school textbooks praising Moscow's role in Ukraine.

articles.title: Mexico bans cellphones in schools, despite opposition from parents worried about violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mexican authorities are also preparing to implement regulations this month that will require digital platforms to remove posts containing hate speech, abuse, sexual violence, harassment, cyberbullying and other illegal content

Starting Tuesday, Mexican schools will ban cellphones from classrooms as part of a federal government effort to limit children's and teenagers' use of electronic devices, following similar measures taken by over a hundred countries in the last decade.

The initiative, spearheaded by Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, has been supported by experts who see it as an opportunity to reduce young Mexicans' exposure to technology and the resulting attention deficit, stress and anxiety.

Mexican authorities are also preparing to implement regulations this month that will require digital platforms to remove posts containing hate speech, abuse, sexual violence, harassment, cyberbullying and other illegal content.

However, the cellphone ban, which will take effect on November 3, is already facing resistance in some parts of the country. Some parents fear being unable to communicate with their children amid ongoing violence, from which children and adolescents are not spared.

According to the civil society coalition Network for Children's Rights in Mexico (REDIM), in the first half of this year, one in 10 Mexicans between the ages of 0 and 17 were victims of crimes involving organised crime.

“I don't think parents will accept not giving their children a means of digital communication, especially when those children … are spending so much time at home instead of at school,” said Francisco Ortiz, state representative of the National Union of Parents in Sinaloa, accusing the government of ignoring parents and approving regulations that “go against parental authority, against the rights of parents.”

The decree issued by Sheinbaum prohibits the use of cellphones and electronic devices inside elementary and middle schools throughout the school day, and only allows their use for educational purposes under the guidance of teachers or for personal emergencies, disability and health needs. Students can take their phones with them on the way to school.

Benigno Gomez, a father from Reynosa in the northern state of Tamaulipas, said that while he understood the educational authorities' need to reduce students' time on cellphones, he found it “a little difficult” that they weren't allowed to have a cellphone to deal with a potential risk situation.
Mexican authorities have not commented on these concerns and have instead focused on the harm caused by cellphones.

During a recent address to the Chamber of Deputies, Mexico's Secretary of Public Education, Mario Delgado, stated that the Sheinbaum administration seeks to “prevent addiction to digital platforms and the disorders they cause in minors.”

Just as the sun was beginning to rise, the residents of Escuinapa, the capital of the municipality of the same name located in southern Sinaloa, awoke on the morning of October 22 to alarming news. A bus that regularly travels through the small town -- which relies on mango and shrimp production -- was shot at by a man on a motorcycle.

More than a dozen high school students were on board. A video recorded by one of the passengers circulated on social media, showing children on the floor and others hiding among the seats while one teenager asks another, “Do you have any credit (on your cellphone)?”

articles.title: Approval of India-made version of HIV-prevention shot raises hopes in low-income countries
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Generic lenacapavir should start to become available in some places within weeks

The US Food and Drug Administration has approved an India-made generic version of the world's only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV -- a big step toward making the drug available inexpensively and more quickly in 120 low- and middle-income countries.
The announcement was made on Monday morning by the manufacturer and organisations that helped to speed up development of the medication, called lenacapavir.

The generic was developed by India-based Dr. Reddy's Laboratories under an agreement brokered by Unitaid, the Clinton Health Access Initiative and Wits RHI, a health research institute in Africa. The partners sought to accelerate development and make the drug available at an affordable price.

The drug is expected to cost USD 40 a year per person in the countries where it will be available, the same price as daily preventive pills available now. But the shots are much more convenient than the pills because they're needed much less frequently and they nearly eliminated new infections in two groundbreaking studies of people at high risk.

People don't always take their daily dose of medication, “and if you do not take it, you cannot get protected against HIV,” said Carmen Perez Casas, HIV lead for the grant-making organisation Unitaid, a global health agency. “With lenacapavir, we are much more hopeful.”

Ultimately, advocates said, the medication should help drive down cases of HIV and AIDS -- and deaths. According to the WHO, 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV and 570,000 died from HIV-related causes last year.

With an affordable, high-quality generic medication now available, “we could help to scale this to the 20 million people around the world who need PrEP,” prescription medicine taken by people at risk of HIV before being exposed to the virus, said Carolyn Amole, who leads the HIV programme for the Clinton Health Access Initiative, a global health organisation.
“And if we scale to those levels,” she added, “we can actually begin to bring an end to the HIV epidemic.”

Generic lenacapavir can't be sold in the U.S. because a brand-name version, Yeztugo, made by Gilead Sciences and approved last year, is still protected by a patent. The U.S. list price for that version, meaning the cost before insurance, is USD 28,218 a year. Gilead officials say that's similar to some other types of PrEP, which stands for pre-exposure prophylaxis.

The new generic was approved by the FDA under a longstanding practice designed to ensure the quality of HIV-related drugs provided to other countries by the U.S. government. Approval of a drug by the U.S. FDA can speed regulatory approval in many other countries. The approval is considered “tentative,” the FDA's standard designation for generics while the originator remains under patent.

Until now, Gilead has been the sole supplier of lenacapavir, and demand has outstripped supply in low- and middle-income countries. Last year, Gilead established royalty-free licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers to enable production. Those voluntary licenses cover a specific set of countries in sub-Saharan Africa, Asia and Latin America.

“We share the sense of urgency around expanding access to lenacapavir for HIV prevention,” a Gilead spokesperson said in a statement. “We believe we have enabled the fastest and most sustainable path to expanding access for communities most affected by HIV.”

articles.title: Public office not a consolation prize for defeated politicians: Karnataka High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Court quashes appointment of ex-MLA to land regularisation panel on his own recommendation

The High Court of Karnataka has quashed the constitution of an additional committee for considering applications for the regularisation of unauthorised occupation of government lands in the Byndoor Assembly constituency in Udupi district under the chairmanship of K. Gopal Poojary, former Congress Party MLA, acting on his letter in which he recommended himself for the post of chairperson of the additional committee.

A division bench comprising Justice D.K. Singh and Justice H. Shanthi Bhushan passed the order while allowing an appeal filed by Bydoor constituency’s present MLA, Gururaj Gantihole, who had challenged a single judge’s order dismissing his plea against the constitution of an additional committee headed by Mr. Poojary.

Curiously, the main committee, headed by Mr. Gantihole, for considering such applications was assigned half the number of applications that were assigned to the additional committee headed by Mr. Poojary, the Bench noted.

The Bench pointed out that Mr. Poojary had written a letter in November 2023 to the then Udupi district in-charge Minister, stating that over 33,000 such applications are pending in the Assembly constituency and even recommended the names of three persons for the posts of members of the additional committee while proposing himself for the post of its chairperson.

The then district in-charge Minister had forwarded Mr. Poojary’s letter to the then Revenue Minister. Acting on his instructions, the government, on December 4, 2023, constituted the additional committee as desired by Mr. Poojary and made him chairperson of the additional committee.

However, the Bench noted that though the Karnataka Land Revenue Act allows the constitution of an additional committee, with the main committee headed by the MLA of the respective constituency, the government independently assessed the need for an additional committee but merely acted on Mr. Poojary’s letter.

The Bench also observed that power was entrusted to public authorities to serve the people, “not to provide a refuge for those who have lost their political standing. Public office cannot be treated as a consolation prize for a defeated politician, nor can it be converted into a reward for political loyalty.”

“...after failing to secure election as MLA from the Byndoor constituency, Mr. Poojary sought to obtain a position of authority through the constitution of an additional committee by making a request to the then Minister for Revenue... What could not be secured through the election appears to have been pursued through an indirect route. The additional committee was intended to serve the statutory purpose of considering applications for grant of land. Its constitution cannot be founded on a defeated politician’s personal desire to acquire power or office,” the Bench observed.

Meanwhile, the Bench directed the government to frame guidelines for appointing a chairperson to the additional committee to ensure that appointments were made on relevant considerations and in furtherance of the statutory purpose, without being influenced by extraneous or personal considerations.

fullParagraphs: TDP emerges as the largest constituent, winning 118 wards and leading in another 21, while Jana Sena secures 26 wards across the three districts

The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), comprising the Telugu Desam Party (TDP), Jana Sena Party (JSP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), appeared headed for a decisive victory in the urban local body elections in Guntur, Palnadu and Bapatla districts, with the alliance parties securing leads in most municipalities and the Guntur Municipal Corporation.

In Guntur, TDP mayoral candidate Kovelamudi Lakshmi Aparna was leading against YSRCP candidate Tadikonda Alivelu Nagapadma Sridevi as counting continued. Of the 76 wards in the Guntur Municipal Corporation (GMC), the TDP won 16 and was leading in 21, while the Jana Sena Party won three and was ahead in 10. The BJP and YSRCP won one ward each, with the latter leading in another 10. An Independent candidate also won one ward.

In Tenali, Jana Sena Party candidate Thotakura Venkata Ramana Rao won the chairperson election with 51,020 votes, defeating YSRCP candidate Maddali Seshachalam, who secured 33,927 votes, by a margin of 17,093 votes. The TDP won 29 of the 52 wards, followed by the Jana Sena Party with 16, the YSRCP with six and the BJP with one.

In Bapatla district, TDP chairperson candidate Kurra Avarna was leading against YSRCP candidate Chimatala Lakshmi by 14,319 votes in Repalle as counting continued. The TDP won 25 wards, the Jana Sena Party two, the BJP one, the YSRCP two and an Independent candidate one. Counting in Chirala was suspended in view of Cyclone Murasu.

In Palnadu district, the TDP won 17 wards in Macherla, 13 in Vinukonda and nine each in Sattenapalli and Chilakaluripet. The Jana Sena Party secured six wards, the BJP three and the YSRCP six across the four municipalities. Results of the chairperson elections in all four municipalities were awaited as counting continued.

Across the three districts, the TDP won 118 wards and was leading in another 21. The Jana Sena Party secured 26 wards and was ahead in 10, while the BJP won five. The YSRCP won 15 wards and was leading in another 10. Independents secured two wards.

articles.title: ‘Following situation’: MEA on protests by garment workers in Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The garment workers are holding protests over their demand for higher pay, prompting authorities to deploy additional paramilitary forces after reports surfaced of vandalism and violence
India on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) said it is following the situation arising out of the protests by garment workers in Bangladesh.
The garment workers are holding protests over their demand for higher pay, prompting authorities to deploy additional paramilitary forces after reports surfaced of vandalism and violence.

The latest wave of protests has forced 670 of around 4,000 registered garment factories to shut in Dhaka, Gazipur and central Mymensingh, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA).
"We have been following the situation in Bangladesh. There have been developments there, and we continue to follow those developments," External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.
"As far as the India-Bangladesh relationship is concerned, we want to work towards a positive, forward-looking, and constructive relationship," he said at his regular media briefing.

To a question on the Ganga Water Treaty between India and Bangladesh, Mr. Jaiswal said both sides have a "joint rivers commission, and it is the structured mechanism for discussion on all cross-boundary rivers, including Ganga".
The Ganga water treaty was inked in December 1996 that provides for a mechanism for sharing of the river water between the two riparian states. The treaty expires this year.
Mr. Jaiswal gave an indirect response to a question on whether Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would undertake a visit to India.
"We have already extended an invitation to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh to visit India, and if there is an update, I will keep you informed," he said.

articles.title: Identify children working in garages and bring them back to school, says Mandya Deputy Commissioner
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Special training and remedial teaching measures should be formulated to improve the learning abilities of academically backward children; parents should also be counselled, says DC
Mandya Deputy Commissioner Kumar has instructed officials to identify children from the minority community working in garages and re-enroll them in schools.

Speaking at a meeting to review programmes implemented by various departments under the Prime Minister’s new 15-point programme for welfare of minorities in Mandya on Tuesday, Mr. Kumar emphasised on the need to keep a special vigil to ensure that the education of children from the minority community is not disrupted.
He said the officials should identify children, who drop out of school midway due to economic and social reasons to work in garages and other places, and bring them back to school.
He stated that children who are continuously absent from school must be identified, and the reasons for their absenteeism should be traced.

Special training and remedial teaching measures should be formulated to improve the learning abilities of academically backward children. Along with the children, parents must also be counselled and convinced about the importance of education and the future opportunities provided by higher studies.
“Specifically, if children under the age of 18 are found working in garages, the departments concerned must work in co-ordination to bring them back into the educational mainstream”, he said.
Various loan facilities must reach eligible beneficiaries to ensure the economic self-reliance of the minority community, he said.

The Lead Bank officials should take action to provide necessary credit facilities for housing loans, self-employment, and other economic activities. Along with sanctioning loans to eligible beneficiaries under the PM SVANidhi scheme, skill training should be provided based on their interests and aptitude to encourage them to start their own ventures, he noted.
The Health Department must make necessary preparations to administer the HPV vaccine to girls under the age of 14 from the minority community.
Essential infrastructure, including quality drinking water, cleanliness, and toilets, must be provided in hostels for minority students.

Zilla Panchayat Planning Cell Officer Dhanush, District Officer of the Minority Welfare Department Madhushree, District Family Welfare Officer G.S. Bettaswamy, Joint Director of the Agriculture Department Jayaswamy G.S., and officials from various other departments were present at the meeting.

articles.title: Municipal verdict a mandate to serve more, says HRD Minister Nara Lokesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TDP-led coalition is accepting the results with humility as people’s blessing for the good governance, he avers
IT & HRD Minister Nara Lokesh has said that the municipal polls verdict is a mandate to serve but not to celebrate.

In a post on X on Tuesday, Mr. Lokesh said the TDP-led coalition was accepting it with humility as the people’s blessing for the good governance of the last two-and-a-half years. He congratulated the victorious TDP, Jana Sena and BJP candidates, and leaders and workers for their collective efforts.

“Now that the municipal elections are over, our only focus is service, for every citizen, beyond party lines. There is no room for arrogance. Keeping the trust people placed in us is our real responsibility, and we will work harder than ever to deliver on their aspirations,” he added.

articles.title: NMDC’s iron ore output rose 18% in Oct, sales dip amid rain impact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Dispatches were temporarily impacted by disruptions to the Kottavalasa–Kirandul (KK) railway line after sections of the route were washed away due to heavy monsoon rains in September and October.
State-owned NMDC reported October iron ore production rose 18% year-on-year (YoY) to 5.04 million tonnes, while sales declined more than 11% to 3.44 MT.
For the seven months ended October, production stood at 32.32 MT (26.47 MT) and sales 25.67 MT (26.12 MT).

The company said dispatches were temporarily impacted by disruptions to the Kottavalasa–Kirandul (KK) railway line after sections of the route were washed away due to heavy monsoon rains in September and October. The disruption affected evacuation from NMDC’s Bailadila mines in Chhattisgarh for nearly a month.
With rail connectivity restored and supplies resumed, it expects the dispatches and sales to improve in the coming months, NMDC said.

“The 18% growth in iron ore production in October reflects the sustained efforts of the teams. With the rail connectivity restored and supplies resumed, we expect dispatches and sales to improve in the coming months,” CMD Amitava Mukherjee said. NMDC is eyeing 60 MT production this fiscal and becoming a 100 MT mining company by 2030.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Elections 2026 LIVE: Trump says midterm results will be ‘better than you think’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats, and governorships in 36 States are up for election, with about 210 million people registered to vote
US President Donald Trump said Tuesday (November 3, 2026), that Republicans would perform “better than you think” in the midterm elections.
He declared that “inflation is solved” and “everything’s going good”, despite continued voter concerns over the cost of groceries, fuel and healthcare.

Inflation is running at 3.7% annually, up from 3% when Mr. Trump began his second term. In an interview with Fox & Friends, Mr. Trump did not address concerns over prices, instead highlighting immigration enforcement and expanding US manufacturing.
Democrat James Talarico is making an ambitious bid to win a Texas Senate seat for his party for the first time since 1988.
He is challenging Republican Ken Paxton, whose record has been marked by ethical questions and a statehouse impeachment over corruption allegations.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said higher fuel prices are linked to the conflict in Iran and urged Republicans to be honest with voters. He said blaming former President Joe Biden for the increase would amount to “gaslighting” working-class people.
Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces an unusually strong challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton, a megachurch pastor who has made affordability a key issue.
A Democrat has not won a Senate race in Kansas in 94 years, and the contest has set a state record for campaign advertising spending.
Susan Myers (60), a voter in Falmouth, said she is hopeful that Democrat Troy Jackson can defeat Republican Sen. Susan Collins, but wary after recent disappointments.
“I feel like there’s been so much disappointment these last few election cycles that I don’t want to get my hopes up,” she said.
Iowa’s top of the ticket is up for grabs after Republican Governor Kim Reynolds and Senator Joni Ernst opted out of reelection bids.

articles.title: Iran president says return to war benefits 'no one', after reported U.S. strikes
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: It came as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump's grip on power
Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that a return to war would benefit "no one", hours after reported U.S. strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.
It came as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterm elections that threaten President Donald Trump's grip on power.

Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the U.S., Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said the Islamic republic was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", while deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran retained the right to "legitimate self-defence" after the strikes.

But Mr. Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue", adding that "no one will benefit from this war" if it reignited, and emphasising that the country's supreme leader had recently granted the government new powers to negotiate issues previously "off-limits".

The U.S. strikes, reported by The Wall Street Journal, CNN, The New York Times and other outlets, hit Qeshm island in the Hormuz waterway, a key flashpoint of the Middle East war that has upended global markets.
Unnamed U.S. officials cited by the outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature. The Journal said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes.
U.S. Central Command did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.
The U.S. and Israel launched their war with Iran with a massive wave of strikes in late February. The conflict has been stalemated for months.
Asked if Israel was involved in the latest reported strikes, an Israeli military spokesperson told AFP , "No".

The reported Qeshm attack came just hours after Mr. Trump signalled a deal with Iran "could happen", as U.S. voters prepared to cast their ballots in midterms dominated by public dissatisfaction with the war and the inflation it has brought.
"Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible," Mr. Trump posted on his Truth Social platform.
Iranian state news agency IRNA reported five explosions in rapid succession on Qeshm island, and that some residents reported seeing two aircraft flying in its skies.

articles.title: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Teams of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha

The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 31 on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), with dozens of people still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.

Teams of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find more than 45 missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting.

“The scale of the tragedy is terrifying,” Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region's military administration, wrote in an online post. “This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war.”

Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

“The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs,” he said. “But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes.”
Three days of mourning were declared in Zaporizhzhia, where Russian bunker-busting bombs, filled with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives, were used in Monday's (November 2) attack.
The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Mr. Semikin said on Tuesday (November 3). At least five people were hurt.
In the northeast region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said.

A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients were transferred to other medical facilities, head of the regional military administration Oleh Syniehubov said.
In the Dnipro area, rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble on Tuesday (November 3) morning, after a Russian attack killed one person and wounded 17, local authorities said.
The attack damaged an outpatient clinic and a hospital. Patients were transferred to other hospitals, Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said.

Moscow kept up its nightly attacks on power plants and energy infrastructure ahead of winter, causing extensive damage and electricity outages as it carried out 20 strikes in 10 regions overnight, Ukraine's energy ministry said.

articles.title: U.S. Midterm Election night agenda: When polls close and when to expect results
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: With voters deciding thousands of races across the country, keeping track of which races to watch throughout the night and when to expect results can get tricky
With voters deciding thousands of races across the United States on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), keeping track of the contests to watch and when results may arrive can be tricky.
Here is a rundown of the major races, hour by hour, and an indication of how long vote-counting may take.

4:30 a.m: The first polls of the night close in most of Indiana and Kentucky, but statewide winners will not be declared in either state until the last polls close at 5:30 a.m. Winners could be declared in the states’ easternmost congressional districts.
Key contests include competitive U.S. House races in Indiana’s 5th and Kentucky’s 6th congressional districts.

5:30 a.m: .All polls close in six states, including Georgia, South Carolina and Virginia, which typically complete most of their vote counting on election night. In the 2024 general election, vote counting in all three states reached the halfway mark during the 8 p.m. hour.

The counts were 90% complete at 8:51 a.m. in Georgia, 9:44 a.m. in South Carolina and 10:37 a.m. in Virginia. The Associated Press (AP) declared Republican Donald Trump the winner of Georgia’s competitive presidential contest at 11:28 a.m.
Most Florida polls also close at 5:30 a.m., including those in every competitive congressional district. Statewide winners will not be declared until polls close in the Central Time Zone at 6:30 a.m.

6:00 a.m.: Polls close in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia. All three states counted votes relatively quickly in 2024, reaching the halfway point at about 7:30 a.m. and roughly 90% by the 9:30 a.m. hour. The AP declared a winner in Ohio’s competitive 2024 U.S. Senate race at 9:57 a.m.

Key contests include U.S. Senate races in Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio; gubernatorial races in Georgia and Ohio; and U.S. House races in Florida, Indiana, South Carolina, Virginia, Ohio and North Carolina.
6:30 a.m.: This is prime time on election night, with polls fully or partially closing in nearly half the states, including Florida, Maine, New Hampshire and Pennsylvania.
Florida typically counts votes quickly, with results from much of the state beginning to come in during the 5:30 a.m. hour. In 2024, 90% of the vote had been counted by 6:37 a.m.

In 2024, vote counts in New Hampshire and Pennsylvania reached the halfway mark at 8:42 a.m. They reached 90% at 12:12 p.m. in New Hampshire and 11:18 a.m. in Pennsylvania. Maine did not reach the halfway mark until 12:54 a.m.

articles.title: Students blockade dozens of French schools and universities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: After returning from a two-week autumn break, some students resumed their protest campaign on November 2

Students blockaded dozens of high schools and universities across France on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike.

After returning from a two-week autumn break, some students resumed their protest campaign on Monday (November 2), calling on the authorities to renovate dilapidated schools, reduce class sizes and create more university places.

Authorities said on Tuesday (November 3) that 48 out of France's 3,700 high schools were blocked amid tight security, including in Paris, Rennes and Lyon. The USL student union said 500 schools were blocked.
Fifty-one higher education institutions out of 184 were also disrupted, officials said.
The USL union denounced what it called heavy-handed tactics, with "young people pinned against walls and riot police units deployed" outside schools.
A union representative said the authorities appeared to want to blunt a new day of blockades when trade unions have called a nationwide strike.
"We don't even have the right to vote, we can't do anything, so this is our only way of expressing ourselves," a high school student in northwestern Paris said on condition of anonymity.
Thousands of students also marched in Paris and several other cities.
Education Minister Edouard Geffray spoke out against the action, saying students needed to study and prepare for exams.
"Preventing them from entering their school deprives them of a fundamental right: the right to an education," he said on X, adding that some staff members had "once again been subjected to violence".
In the northwestern city of Rennes, around 30 students blocked the Brequigny High School, one of the country's largest secondary schools.
Tensions quickly flared between students and the school administration.

The minister has been present in Assam for the last four days to monitor the tigress.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore. "She is not the property of any government. Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, but there have been no reports of a tiger’s presence in the region of late. articles.title: Slow recovery: On the ISRO’s GSLV-F18 mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: ISRO needs more human and material resources to fulfil its mandate

With the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission and the NVS-03 satellite’s healthy status , the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is on course to heave a sigh of relief. Its last 18 months have been constrained by the consequences of two launch failures involving PSLV rockets , which share some of their design aspects with GSLV, to the extent that the F18 mission was only the second successful launch of 2026. If the NVS-03 satellite is successfully manoeuvred into its final intended orbital slot and commissioned, ISRO will also have pulled off a rescue mission for the ‘Navigation with Indian Constellation’ (NavIC) programme , which has been at least one functional satellite short for the last six months and thus unable to meet its primary purpose of providing standalone positioning services over the Indian subcontinent. The three second-generation NVS satellites thus far are distinguished by having at least one indigenously made atomic clock onboard, in line with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee (PSC) on Science and Technology and India’s investments in quantum timekeeping, and away from the imported clocks onboard the first-generation IRNSS satellites.

The PSC had also flagged procurement bottlenecks across ISRO’s programmes, including difficulties with obtaining specialised components and ensuring vendor readiness on the timelines that NavIC needs. The ISRO Space Applications Centre’s ‘request for proposals’ in 2025 also specified a large lead time of nearly two years between a contract’s start and the first two flight models. The Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and the programme to modernise the Semiconductor Laboratory can be tweaked to serve these needs, with the Electronics Ministry also setting aside dedicated funds for developing specialised components and their qualification tests in a five- to seven-year programme. In tandem, the government must allocate around ₹17,000 crore in the 2027-28 Union Budget for the Department of Space, against ₹13,705.6 crore in 2026-27, with the hike focusing on manufacturing launch vehicles, replacing satellites, and recruitment. Besides, NavIC also requires a dedicated operator, so that ISRO can be left to focus on its core mandate, and India needs a national space law addressing private participation in this enterprise, and liability. Two successful orbital missions in five-sixths of a year is unbecoming of a national space programme with imminent plans of human spaceflight, a space station, and reusable launch vehicle capabilities. Without significant measures, ISRO will lurch from one mission to the next as and when its inadequate workforce is able to make do with its inadequate allocation.

articles.title: Dwindling support: On the U.S. and the Cuban embargo
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India and the world must stand up against the bullying of Cuba by the U.S.

Nearly every year since 1992, the United Nations General Assembly has passed a resolution calling on the U.S. to end its decades-old economic embargo on Cuba . As a result, the outcome at the UNGA resolution titled the ‘Necessity of ending the economic, commercial and financial embargo imposed by the United States of America against Cuba’ passed on October 30, was expected. Surprisingly, the support for the resolution this year was dramatically lower than previous years. For the preceding decade, more than 180 countries of the 193-member UNGA had expressed their support for ending the embargo, but the numbers dropped to 165 in favour in 2025; this year’s tally dropped sharply lower, with 130 in favour, 25 abstaining and 17 countries voting against the resolution. The trend clearly points to efforts by the Trump administration to use its pressure on countries to change their votes, and many appear to have succumbed to those threats. Among those were several Latin American countries, that have more recently grown closer to the U.S., particularly after the operation in Venezuela in January 2026 , where U.S. marines abducted President Maduro and brought him to the U.S. for a trial. Countries in the region such as Costa Rica, Ecuador, Argentina, and Colombia that have downgraded ties with Havana, switched votes on the resolution. In addition, U.S. diplomats argued that Havana-Moscow ties emboldened Russia’s war in Ukraine , which led to several western countries switching their vote. Diplomats from Ukraine and Poland, for example, referred to Cuba’s ties with Russia while explaining their vote, and Germany and Italy switched for the first time in many years to abstaining on the resolution. While it is clear that the bulk of the Group of 77 and non-aligned states including India maintained their support on the resolution for Cuba, the vote by the others demonstrates a disquieting turn.

Amidst these turns, New Delhi must be credited for standing firm on the issue , opposing the embargo, and calling for “dialogue and diplomacy” in its statement. The vote came a month after the BRICS New Delhi declaration expressed “deep concern” over the tightening of unilateral blockade measures on Cuba, and the “worrying humanitarian impact” on the Cuban people. It is important that India continue to stand up to such unilateral measures and amplify the voice of smaller countries, particularly those in the Global South.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Even as unemployment falls, lack of ‘decent work’ in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth; workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks

I ndia’s unemployment rate fell from 6.1% in 2017-18 to 3.2% in 2023-24. At the same time, female workforce participation increased for the first time in decades as has been widely reported in government documents. In light of these positive developments, it is the right time to ask what kind of jobs have been generated in India recently, and what working conditions accompany them.

This is important because employment alone does not inherently ensure dignity, security, or a stable livelihood. A worker engaged in garment sewing without a formal contract, a gig worker without insurance coverage, or a construction labourer without paid leave may technically be considered employed, but they remain outside the promise of decent work. The International Labour Organization (ILO) defines ‘decent work’ as employment that offers equitable income, workplace rights, social security and dignity. This principle is integrated into Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG-8), which advocates “decent work for all”. Measured this way, India’s labour market persistently exhibits high levels of informality, insecure employment, and increasing inequalities.

Using two rounds of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), 2017-18 and 2023-24, the quality of employment in India has been analysed. By constructing a multidimensional Decent Work Index (DWI) based on three subdimensions — employment status, employment opportunity, and social security — across five major industries (agriculture, manufacturing, construction, wholesale and retail, and transport), it was observed that India has made progress in improving work conditions over time. The overall DWI increased from 0.247 in 2017-18 to 0.302 in 2023-24. While this indicates some improvement in job quality, the overall level remains alarmingly low. More importantly, progress has been uneven across sectors, regions, gender and caste groups.

Manufacturing in the secondary sector and transport in the tertiary sector showed the highest improvement in decent work conditions during this period. The manufacturing sector’s DWI increased from 0.324 to 0.411 due to a gradual rise in formalisation and digitalisation. The transport sector also experienced significant progress (from 0.285 to 0.35), largely due to the expansion of urban logistics and app-based platform work.

However, these improvements also reveal an important concern. Even in sectors where employment conditions have improved, access to social security remains limited. A large number of workers still do not have written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or insurance coverage. Though employment opportunities are increasing, labour protections and job security are not improving at the same pace. Agriculture, which continues to employ the largest share of India’s workforce, remains the lowest-quality employment generating sector. The agricultural sector’s DWI marginally increased from 0.211 to 0.267 during the study period; most agricultural workers continue to be self-employed or unpaid family workers without stable income or labour protections. The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). It has expanded into supply chains, app-based work in the gig and platform economy, logistics, home-based production, and in even organised industries through contractualisation and outsourcing.

The challenge becomes even more serious when viewed in the context of social inequality. The analysis by the authors shows that decent work outcomes improve significantly with education, formal enterprise employment and skill training. However, informalisation of jobs reduces decent work creation in India over time. Especially concerning is the growing intersection of caste and gender disadvantage: women from Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes experienced a decline in decent-work outcomes between 2017-18 and 2023-24, even as outcomes for men improved. The labour market penalty for being both female and socially marginalised has intensified after the COVID-19 pandemic. This shows that inequality in India’s labour market is not just economic, it is also structurally rooted in caste and gender hierarchies.

Regional disparities further expose the uneven nature of labour market progress. States such as Goa, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana perform substantially better in terms of decent-work creation; in contrast, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh continue to lag behind.
The findings point to a serious policy concern: while India has been able to create more jobs, it is still struggling to ensure that these jobs provide decent working conditions and security.

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth. Workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks. Moreover, informality depresses productivity, weakens tax capacity, and increases inequality. India cannot measure labour market success only through reduction in unemployment rates and income growth. A country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047 cannot rely indefinitely on insecure, low-paid and unprotected labour. Economic growth without decent work can create a workforce that may have jobs, but still lives with insecurity, instability and a lack of protection. India has to shift from a ‘job-counting approach’ to a ‘job-quality approach’.

The findings point toward where policy should focus. First, social protection must extend to all workers — gig and platform workers, self-employed, farmers, and informal workers — through systems that are portable and accessible regardless of employment status. Platforms such as e-Shram are a good start, but registering alone does not guarantee protection; workers need real protection, not just a database entry.

Second, formalisation policies should focus on labour conditions, not just business registration. Enterprises receiving tax incentives or subsidies should be linked to mandatory worker protections such as written contracts, paid leave, and social security contributions.

The issue is not merely low productivity; rather it is the rise of informal jobs. Construction and retail sectors tell a similar story. Workers remain dependent on casual employment, subcontracting chains and insecure labour arrangements. Welfare schemes exist on paper but implementation gaps continue to exclude millions of workers.

Nearly 90% of India’s workforce remains informally employed, a share that has risen since 2019, according to the India Employment Report 2024 (ILO–IHD). It has expanded into supply chains, app-based work in the gig and platform economy, logistics, home-based production, and in even organised industries through contractualisation and outsourcing.

The challenge becomes even more serious when viewed in the context of social inequality. The analysis by the authors shows that decent work outcomes improve significantly with education, formal enterprise employment and skill training. However, informalisation of jobs reduces decent work creation in India over time. Especially concerning is the growing intersection of caste and gender disadvantage: women from Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes experienced a decline in decent-work outcomes between 2017-18 and 2023-24, even as outcomes for men improved. The labour market penalty for being both female and socially marginalised has intensified after the COVID-19 pandemic. This shows that inequality in India’s labour market is not just economic, it is also structurally rooted in caste and gender hierarchies.

Regional disparities further expose the uneven nature of labour market progress. States such as Goa, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, and Haryana perform substantially better in terms of decent-work creation; in contrast, Bihar, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh continue to lag behind.

The findings point to a serious policy concern: while India has been able to create more jobs, it is still struggling to ensure that these jobs provide decent working conditions and security.

Poor-quality employment generation has consequences for economic growth. Workers without social security spend less, save less and remain vulnerable to economic shocks. Moreover, informality depresses productivity, weakens tax capacity, and increases inequality. India cannot measure labour market success only through reduction in unemployment rates and income growth. A country aspiring to become Viksit Bharat by 2047 cannot rely indefinitely on insecure, low-paid and unprotected labour. Economic growth without decent work can create a workforce that may have jobs, but still lives with insecurity, instability and a lack of protection. India has to shift from a ‘job-counting approach’ to a ‘job-quality approach’.

The findings point toward where policy should focus. First, social protection must extend to all workers — gig and platform workers, self-employed, farmers, and informal workers — through systems that are portable and accessible regardless of employment status. Platforms such as e-Shram are a good start, but registering alone does not guarantee protection; workers need real protection, not just a database entry.

Second, formalisation policies should focus on labour conditions, not just business registration. Enterprises receiving tax incentives or subsidies should be linked to mandatory worker protections such as written contracts, paid leave, and social security contributions.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu LIVE update: Orange alert in six Telangana districts, yellow alert in five; holiday announced for schools, colleges in T.N., A.P. districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclonic storm lay centred about 350 km east of Chennai, 400 km east-southeast of Nellore, 430 km southeast of Machilipatnam, 420 km east-southeast of Kavali, 450 km southeast of Ongole, and 520 km south of Visakhapatnam, according to IMD.
Chennai District Collector S. Malathi Helen and Tiruvallur District Collector S. Kavitha last night announced a holiday for schools and colleges on Monday.

According to data from the Regional Meteorological Centre here, till 10.30 p.m. on Sunday, in Chennai district, the Nungambakkam station recorded 20.4 mm of rainfall, Meenambakkam recorded 4.9 mm, YMCA Nandanam recorded 13.5 mm, Ennore Port 39 mm, Madhavaram 21 mm, Anna University 10.5 mm and Taramani 7.5 mm.
In Tiruvallur district, Puzhal recorded 11 mm, Poonamallee 0.5 mm, and in Chengalpattu district, VIT Chennai recorded 0.5 mm of rainfall.

In the wake of the cyclone, Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu today called Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to seek assistance from the T.N. government for the restoration of power systems, according to the A.P. CM office.
Mr. Naidu requested that manpower and machinery be sent for restoration, as a large number of power poles were damaged due to the Murasu cyclone.
Mr. Vijay has reportedly responded positively to the request.
Palnadu District Collector Kritika Shukla has announced holiday for all government and private schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday (November 2) in view of Cyclone Murasu.

articles.title: Rebel leaders of AIADMK do not take part in district secretaries’ meeting chaired by Palaniswami
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting

The rebel leaders in the AIADMK, S.P. Velumani and Natham R. Viswanathan, did not take part in the meeting of party’s district secretaries chaired by general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami at the party head office in Chennai on Sunday.

The party’s performance in the recent bypoll in Dharapuram and Madurantakam Assembly constituencies, and preparations for its general council and executive committee meetings, expected to be conducted in December this year, were among the issues discussed at the meeting. Senior leaders A. Tamilmagan Hussain, K.P. Munusamy, and Dindigul C. Sreenivasan were among those who attended the meeting.

Earlier, Mr. Palaniswami issued a statement criticising the TVK-led government over the rates of medicines in Mudhalvar Marundhagams (formerly Amma Marundhagams). Citing a report from the All India Drug Action Network, he said medicines at Amma Marundhagams were being sold at rates higher than the prices fixed, which is affecting the poor.
Retired Additional Superintendent of Police S. Velladurai, who was known for his involvement in many ‘police encounter’ cases, joined the AIADMK in the presence of Mr. Palaniswami on Sunday.

articles.title: Litigants will not be entitled to refund of court fees if disputes get settled out of court after commencement of trial, rules Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji refuses to follow Supreme Court’s 2017 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case and instead follows the top court’s 2010 judgment in Afcons Infrastructure case

Litigants will not be entitled to return of court fees if their civil disputes lead to an out of the court settlement after the commencement of trial in civil suits, the Madras High Court has held after refusing to follow the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the 2021 M.C. Subramaniam’s case.

Justice P.B. Balaji agreed with Advocate General (A-G) Vijay Narayan that the 2021 verdict in M.C. Subramaniam’s case had not factored in the top court’s 2010 judgement passed by a bench of co-equal strength in Afcons Infrastruture Limited versus Cherian Varkey Construction Company Private Limited.

“It is settled law that when there is an earlier ratio of a Coordinate Bench, it is binding on a later Bench of equal strength and if at all the later Bench is not agreeable to the ratio laid down in the earlier decision, it is only open to the later Bench to refer the matter to a larger Bench and not take a contrary view,” the judge said.
He went on to state: “In such view of the matter, I am emboldened to follow and rely upon the ratio laid down in Afcons case instead of following the ratio laid down in M.C.Subramaniam’s case.”

The judge said, the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 insists upon litigants to pay court fees for a reason. The court fee gets collected to meet all necessary and incidental expenses relating to provision of infrastructure for courts, conduct of trials, payment of salaries and allowances to the court staff and so on.

Section 69 of the 1955 Act, as it stood originally, provided for refund of 50% of court fees “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.” In 2007, Section 69A was introduced to the Act providing for refund of 100% of the court fees if the dispute gets settled after the court concerned refers the matter for arbitration, mediation, conciliation, Lok Adalat or such other alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC).

In 2017, the Act was amended again to provide for return of 100% court fees under Section 69 too. However, even then, the legislature consciously did not tinker with the words “whenever any suit is dismissed as settled out of court before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim.”

Further, Justice Balaji highlighted that the Supreme Court in Afcons Infrastructure case had held that the civil courts could refer disputes to the ADR mechanisms mentioned in Section 89 of CPC only before commencement of trial because otherwise, the litigants could use it as a ruse to protract the trial.

Therefore, the continued existence of Section 69 along with the words “before any evidence has been recorded on the merits of the claim” and the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling that courts could refer civil disputes for ADR only before commencement of trial would make it clear that litigants would not be entitled to refund of court fees after the trial commences, the judge held.

The verdict was passed while dismissing two civil revision petitions filed by different litigants. The first civil revision petition had been filed against the order passed by a district court in Tiruvallur district to refund only 50% of court fees and the second had been filed against Chengalpattu court’s order that the litigant would not be entitled to refund of the entire amount of ₹2.54 lakh paid towards court fees.

Justice Balaji held that both the petitioners would not be entitled to refund of any amount of court fees since the out of court settlement had been reached only after commencement of trial. However, since the State had not filed any revision petition against the order to refund 50% of court fees to the first petitioner, the judge refrained from interfering with the Tiruvallur court’s order.

The judge had requested the A-G to assist him in the case considering the important question of law involved in the case related to the State exchequer and recorded the court’s “deep appreciations” to him. He also appreciated senior counsel S. Parthasarathy and S. Subbiah, amicus curiae S. Suresh Sampath, advocates S. Ramesh, S.R. Sundar, A.V. Arun and all other Bar members who made their submissions following an open invitation extended to all of them.

articles.title: BJP alleges rift between Rahul, Priyanka; accuses LoP of sidelining sister at INDIA bloc protests
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Yesterday, during the mock Parliament organised by the Congress party and led by Rahul Gandhi, I observed one thing: Priyanka Vadra was not given an opportunity to speak by Rahul Gandhi or the Congress party,’ said Sambit Patra

The BJP on Sunday (November 1, 2026) claimed the Congress has split into two camps led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and that she was not "allowed" to speak at the two INDIA bloc protests as the Leader of Opposition feared getting sidelined by his sister.

In a video message on Instagram, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra said Priyanka Gandhi's "vote has also been stolen" within the Gandhi family and claimed she appeared unhappy at the mock parliament and the Ramlila Maidan rally.

The INDIA bloc on Saturday (October 31, 2026) held a symbolic "public impeachment" of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the right to vote was under threat as the poll panel was functioning at the behest of the Modi government.
On Sunday (November 1, 2026), the Opposition grouping held a mammoth rally at Ramlila Maidan here against alleged electoral irregularities and voter list revision.

articles.title: NTK cadre want Seeman to seek AIADMK, DMK support for Ambasamudram byelection
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: His decision to contest is being seen as ‘bold’ and has reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections

NTK chief coordinator Seeman’s decision to contest in the Ambasamudram Assembly bypoll (when notified) has set off a debate among the party’s senior office-bearers whether it should seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK for fielding him as the “common candidate”.

A senior party office-bearer said Mr. Seeman had been facing “pressure” internally to reach out to the leadership of the DMK and the AIADMK and ask for support. “Though it is a longshot, our office-bearers are putting pressure on him to reach out to the other parties. Mr. Seeman has explained to them that such a move would go against the fundamental position of the NTK,” an office-bearer said.

Mr. Seeman’s decision to contest was being seen as “bold” and had reportedly energised the cadre after a disappointing showing in this year’s Assembly elections, which saw its vote share reduce by almost half — falling from 8% to around 4%.
Mr. Seeman is yet to win an election despite trying his luck since 2016. A senior member of the party said: “Only a leader who takes these risky moves can keep the party and its cadre with him.”

Regarding the possibility of a common candidate, a party leader admitted it may not “possible” given the current political dynamics in the State. “Our decision to announce that Seeman will contest has given rise to these speculations,” he said.
Party sources said while Mr. Seeman would not formally seek the support of the DMK and the AIADMK, he would nevertheless welcome if “they not contest the elections”.
