articles.title: What are U.S. midterm elections?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. midterm elections on November 3 determine control of Congress, with all 435 House seats, about one-third of the 100 Senate seats, and numerous state governorships up for grabs, in a nationwide vote that weakens or strengthens the President’s agenda depending on which party prevails.

Every four years, halfway through a sitting president’s four-year term, the U.S. holds a nationwide poll known as the midterm elections. Although the White House occupant is not directly up for re-election in this vote, the outcome serves as a de facto referendum on the current administration’s leadership and political agenda.
The legislative branch, the U.S. Congress, is entirely at stake, as voters elect representatives to all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, who serve two-year terms.

At the same time, 35 of the 100 U.S. Senate seats which carry six-year terms are up for grabs (33 regular elections and two special elections in Florida and Ohio) alongside the state gubernatorial seats that decide chief executives across numerous states. articles.title: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The study’s findings about women having a higher prevalence of pain across anatomical sites, resonate with observations from India, say experts, noting that even so, women’s pain has historically been under-recognised, misunderstood, or inadequately treated

Women are more likely than men to report pain across every one of the 11 anatomical sites examined in a global study involving more than 6.1 million people across 118 countries. The study found that differences were particularly pronounced for facial pain, headaches and abdominal pain.

Published in Nature Medicine , the study found that women had 83% higher relative prevalence of facial pain, 74% higher prevalence of headaches and 60% higher prevalence of stomach or abdominal pain than men. Women were also more likely to report high-intensity and widespread pain, highlighting a disparity that extends beyond the occurrence of pain to its severity and distribution.

Science, Space & Environment Report: What a new global study on pain reveals about women’s experiences. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

articles.title: Shock and regret: scientists react to AI roiling life’s work
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis
For decades, three computer scientists built their careers around an idea about the limits of what computers can do.
Artificial intelligence may now have shown it to be wrong: OpenAI and Anthropic each said last week that one of their AI models had disproved the exponential time hypothesis (ETH).
The hypothesis holds that some problems are so hard that computers can solve them only by trying nearly every possible answer. Hundreds of studies in computer science and biology rely on it.

The claim is the latest in a string of AI results that have shaken academia, setting off soul-searching, most notably among mathematicians, over the value of human expertise and the future of their profession.

Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi of the University of California San Diego first proposed the hypothesis around 25 years ago. Ryan Williams of MIT, a leading researcher in the field, had long publicly doubted it. The three are now helping organise an independent review of the claims from the AI companies.
Q: How did you feel when you learned that a machine may have overturned this hypothesis?
Ryan Williams: I did not fully believe the hypothesis, and I’m on the record as a prominent sceptic. So I felt vindicated.

Russell Impagliazzo: I’m afraid I am less cheerful about this than the others. I would have much preferred it to be discovered by a human who could explain their thought process. And I’d like to have shaken the (actual) hand of the person who disproved ETH.
Q: What is left for human researchers facing the machine? What would you tell a student?

Paturi: These breakthroughs extend the frontier of research, but I believe shaping that frontier and moving it forward remain within human capacity and creativity. I would encourage young students to join. They should learn to use these tools while developing their own judgment.

Williams: I think we’re starting to experience a major revolution in the field, and it is absolutely worth going into. Some people may not want to work in the field anymore; others may now feel motivated to.

Impagliazzo: I’m less confident. The rate of change is amazing. Until now, the same researchers mostly did both the glamorous part of research, solving, and the less glamorous part, verifying and explaining. Now it looks like much or most of the first will be done by AI, leaving humans the second -- until next year, when AI progresses further. I have no idea what research will be like next year.

articles.title: Naidu asks NDA leaders to focus on winning MPTC, ZPTC polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister urges alliance partners to ensure heavy polling on November 5, maintain restraint during counting of urban local body votes on November 3
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said elections to the urban local bodies were conducted peacefully despite alleged attempts by the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) to create disturbances.

He asked leaders of the alliance parties to exercise restraint and take adequate precautions during the counting of votes for the urban local body elections on November 3 and polling for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs) on November 5.

Addressing a teleconference with senior leaders of the NDA partners on Monday, Mr. Naidu said the MPTC and ZPTC elections were crucial for the development of rural local bodies, including Zilla and Mandal Parishads. He called upon the alliance leaders to work towards winning the maximum number of seats in all 28 districts.
He said the coalition government had undertaken large-scale development programmes in villages and ensured the welfare of every family, with a focus on good governance.

The NDA should be in power not only at the Centre and in the State but also at the local level to ensure development, he said. Claiming that works worth nearly ₹1.50 lakh crore were under way in rural areas, he urged the alliance leaders to strengthen their presence in local bodies.
Noting the low voter turnout in the urban local body elections, Mr. Naidu asked leaders of the TDP and its allies to work towards ensuring a higher turnout in the MPTC and ZPTC elections.
Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar represented the Jana Sena Party at the teleconference, while BJP State president P.V.N. Madhav also participated.

articles.title: Here are the big stories from Karnataka today
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Welcome to the Karnataka Today newsletter, your guide from The Hindu on the major news stories to follow today. Curated and written by Nalme Nachiyar.

The Central Crime Branch of Bengaluru police on November 2 searched the residence and office of Power TV Managing Director Rakesh Shetty in connection with the alleged fabrication and circulation of a sting video allegedly targeting former chief minister Siddaramaiah. The searches were carried out by multiple teams of investigators after obtaining a search warrant from a court.

Shetty is a key suspect in the case and, along with expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, is accused of being involved in the creation of the allegedly fabricated video. The searches come a day after the CCB disclosed that the mobile phone used to upload the controversial sting video had allegedly changed hands at the official New Delhi residence of Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy.

Karnataka’s Home Minister Priyank Kharge has alleged that a Union Minister is pressuring the Centre to use the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) and Income Tax Department against him and his Cabinet colleagues on the pretext of an investigation into the alleged irregularities in recruitment by the KPSC.

In a post on X, Mr. Kharge alleged that the Union Minister is attempting to use the agencies to implicate Congress leaders in the KPSC recruitment case. He accused what he described as the RSS’s ‘newest Group D recruit’ of trying to pressure all the accused through the ED to falsely name Congress leaders and him in the case.

The Karnataka government has issued the final notification for acquiring the remaining 1,895 acres of land in Bidadi for the Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township (GBIT) project, also known as the Bidadi township project, amid sustained protests by farmers. The fresh notification covers the Bairamangala and Kanchugaranahalli revenue villages on the outskirts of Bengaluru.

With this, the final notification process has been completed for all nine revenue villages, spanning 7,343 acres. The project requires a total of 9,640 acres. The remaining land is owned by the government of Karnataka. The farmers, however, are unhappy with the latest development and have accused the State Government of ‘backstabbing’.

Indian Coast Guard (ICG), District Headquarter 3, Mangaluru, safely evacuated a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention from a fishing vessel sailing about 100 km off Mangaluru coast on November 1 night. The headquarters received a distress call over VHF from Indian Fishing Boat (IFB) Shiv Sagar, about a fisherman who had fallen overboard while hauling fishing nets.

The ICG deployed Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448, which located the fishing boat amid the darkness of the night. The disoriented fisherman, identified as Komara Ramu, was safely evacuated, provided immediate first aid, and transferred to New Mangalore Port Authority jetty. He was subsequently shifted to the nearest hospital for further medical management.

The Karnataka Examination Authority has decided to go ahead with the written examination for direct recruitment to the post of principal of government PU colleges as scheduled on November 20 and 22. The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month.

The KEA is conducting the examination for direct recruitment of government PU college lecturers to 216 vacant posts of Grade A government PU college principal. Lecturers who have served in a college for more than 10 years are qualified to appear for the examination.

Here are the big stories from Karnataka today

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

Welcome to the Karnataka Today newsletter, your guide from The Hindu on the major news stories to follow today. Curated and written by Nalme Nachiyar.

The Central Crime Branch of Bengaluru police on November 2 searched the residence and office of Power TV Managing Director Rakesh Shetty in connection with the alleged fabrication and circulation of a sting video allegedly targeting former chief minister Siddaramaiah. The searches were carried out by multiple teams of investigators after obtaining a search warrant from a court.

Shetty is a key suspect in the case and, along with expelled Congress leader Kripa Alva, is accused of being involved in the creation of the allegedly fabricated video. The searches come a day after the CCB disclosed that the mobile phone used to upload the controversial sting video had allegedly changed hands at the official New Delhi residence of Union Minister H. D. Kumaraswamy.

Karnataka’s Home Minister Priyank Kharge has alleged that a Union Minister is pressuring the Centre to use the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) and Income Tax Department against him and his Cabinet colleagues on the pretext of an investigation into the alleged irregularities in recruitment by the KPSC.

In a post on X, Mr. Kharge alleged that the Union Minister is attempting to use the agencies to implicate Congress leaders in the KPSC recruitment case. He accused what he described as the RSS’s ‘newest Group D recruit’ of trying to pressure all the accused through the ED to falsely name Congress leaders and him in the case.

The Karnataka government has issued the final notification for acquiring the remaining 1,895 acres of land in Bidadi for the Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township (GBIT) project, also known as the Bidadi township project, amid sustained protests by farmers. The fresh notification covers the Bairamangala and Kanchugaranahalli revenue villages on the outskirts of Bengaluru.

With this, the final notification process has been completed for all nine revenue villages, spanning 7,343 acres. The project requires a total of 9,640 acres. The remaining land is owned by the government of Karnataka. The farmers, however, are unhappy with the latest development and have accused the State Government of ‘backstabbing’.

Indian Coast Guard (ICG), District Headquarter 3, Mangaluru, safely evacuated a fisherman in urgent need of medical attention from a fishing vessel sailing about 100 km off Mangaluru coast on November 1 night. The headquarters received a distress call over VHF from Indian Fishing Boat (IFB) Shiv Sagar, about a fisherman who had fallen overboard while hauling fishing nets.

The ICG deployed Indian Coast Guard Ship C-448, which located the fishing boat amid the darkness of the night. The disoriented fisherman, identified as Komara Ramu, was safely evacuated, provided immediate first aid, and transferred to New Mangalore Port Authority jetty. He was subsequently shifted to the nearest hospital for further medical management.

The Karnataka Examination Authority has decided to go ahead with the written examination for direct recruitment to the post of principal of government PU colleges as scheduled on November 20 and 22. The lecturers’ association had submitted a representation seeking postponement of the examination by one month.

The KEA is conducting the examination for direct recruitment of government PU college lecturers to 216 vacant posts of Grade A government PU college principal. Lecturers who have served in a college for more than 10 years are qualified to appear for the examination.

articles.title: Row over special passes to enter Hasanamba Temple in Hassan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging irregularities in the distribution of passes for free darshan during the Hasanamba festival in Hassan, former Minister and JD(S) leader H.D. Revanna has warned that hundreds of party workers would forcefully enter the temple if the issue was not addressed by Tuesday.

Addressing a press conference in Hassan on Sunday, Mr. Revanna alleged that thousands of free passes had been printed and distributed among members of the ruling Congress. He demanded that the district administration make public the details of passes distributed among elected representatives in the district.

Mr. Revanna said an official had come to him to hand over 500 passes, but he refused to accept them. “If the passes are not distributed properly among the elected representatives of the district by Tuesday, I will send 5,000 party workers to barge into the temple,” he said.
He also complained that the district administration had not invited him to the festival.

Excise Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, who is also the Minister in charge of the district, refuted the allegation. “Every legislator has received 500 passes, and Hassan MLA H.P. Swaroop has received 1,500 as the temple is located in his constituency. The Hassan MP has received 1,000. We have streamlined the distribution to avoid the chaos and confusion that arose a couple of years ago over additional passes,” he said.
The Hasanamba festival that began on October 29, will conclude on November 11. The temple is opened for devotees only during this festival, and hence it attracts huge crowd.

articles.title: Man found dead after he kills his wife, two children in Raichur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ​In a tragic incident, a 46-year-old man murdered his wife and two minor children at their residence in Raitha Nagar (Jalal Nagar), Raichur, late on Saturday night, before ending his own life.
​The deceased have been identified as 46-year-old Vishnu, his 36-year-old wife Aruna and their children 10-year-old Shlok and seven-year-old Kushi.
​According to the police, preliminary investigation suggested that Vishnu smothered his wife and children to death while they were asleep.

Following an extensive search operation, police personnel found Vishnu’s body on the railway track near Chikkasugur village in the district where is said to have jumped in front of a train and ended his life.
​Police sources stated that financial distress, exacerbated by severe business losses and unpaid debts, is suspected to be the primary trigger behind the extreme step by Vishnu.

“ Prima facie , financial strain appears to be the reason. However, the exact circumstances leading to the incident will be established only after a comprehensive investigation,” Superintendent of Police Arunangshu Giri said.
​The Market Yard Police have registered a case of murder, while the Railway Police have filed a case in connection with Vishnu’s death.

articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: CM directs officials to brace for flood in Bapatla district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Heavy inflows are expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts for four days

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to take all precautionary measures to prevent loss of life and property in Bapatla district in view of Cyclone Murasu , which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. He reviewed the preparedness of district administrations through a video conference on Monday (November 2, 2026), attended by Bapatla Collector Vinod Kumar V.

The Chief Minister warned that Bapatla was likely to bear the brunt of the cyclone, since heavy inflows of floodwater were expected through irrigation canals from upstream districts, including Guntur, Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram. He asked officials to inspect canal bunds, remain alert for four days of heavy inflows, evacuate people from low-lying areas and establish rehabilitation centres. He also said a special officer would be appointed for Bapatla district.

In a review meeting on cyclone preparedness, Mr. Naidu said the District Collectors should be alert to meet any contingency keeping in view the likelihood of heavy rains and gales. He ordered that steps be taken to fill reservoirs, tanks and ponds through efficient water management in the south coastal and Rayalaseema regions.

కోస్తాంధ్ర తీరానికి అతి దగ్గరగా ఉన్న మురసు తుఫాన్ సన్నద్ధతపై గౌరవ ముఖ్యమంత్రి శ్రీ నారా చంద్రబాబు నాయుడు నేడు సమీక్ష నిర్వహించారు. రియల్ టైమ్ గవర్నెన్స్ సొసైటీ నుంచి క్షేత్రస్థాయిలో తుఫాను సన్నద్ధత గురించి అధికారులు, కలెక్టర్లతో మాట్లాడారు. అర్నబ్ తుఫాను వల్ల జరిగిన విధ్వంసంలో చాలా ప్రాంతాలు సాధారణ స్థితికి వచ్చాయని, మురసు తుఫానును ప్రభావాన్ని కూడా సమర్ధంగా ఎదుర్కోవాల్సి ఉందని అన్నారు. తుఫాను గాలుల కారణంగా దక్షిణ కోస్తాంధ్ర, రాయలసీమ జిల్లాల్లో 8 వేల వరకూ విద్యుత్ స్తంభాలపై ప్రభావం పడే అవకాశం ఉందని అంచనా వేశారు. #AndhraPradesh

Officials told the Chief Minister that heavy rains were expected in south coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema, along with copious inflows into the Nagarjuna Sagar and Pulichintala project catchment areas. They said the impact of Murasu could be less than that of Cyclone Arnab but necessary precautionary steps were being taken.

Mr. Vinod Kumar said the administration had prepared a comprehensive plan involving all departments. Rainfall in the district was 30% below normal, but rain was likely for five days. He said 74 vulnerable locations had been identified, including irrigation canals, roads and tank bunds, where damage was possible. About 1,000 electricity poles and machinery had been kept ready. Weed removal and strengthening of canal bunds were under way.
ALSO WATCH Cyclone Murasu strengthens, heavy rain alerts issued across southern States
He also said 50 personnel had been sent to the Godavari districts to assist in power restoration.

Meanwhile, all government, private and corporate schools, colleges and other educational institutions in Bapatla district would remain closed on November 2 and 3 in view of the forecast of extremely heavy rainfall, the Collector announced.

In an official announcement issued on Monday, the Collector said that extremely heavy rainfall was likely under the influence of the cyclone. He directed the education department officials and managements of all educational institutions to implement the holiday orders immediately. The decision was taken as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of students in view of the anticipated adverse weather conditions.

articles.title: Israel’s intent is to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group: Justice Muralidhar

fullParagraphs: In a strong indictment of Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry, has accused Israel of seeking to expand its occupation while reducing the Palestinian population

Israel’s policy is to maximise the occupation of Palestinian territories and minimise the Palestinian population, says Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, the chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory. articles.title: Ebola reminder of urgent need to finish pandemic treaty: WHO chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people"
Deadly outbreaks like the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo show the urgent need to complete an international pandemic treaty, the World Health Organization chief said Monday.
Wealthy countries and developing nations remain at loggerheads over how an agreement, adopted last year as a framework to handle future Covid-like pandemics, will work in practice.
As the ninth meeting towards finalising the deal opened in Geneva Monday, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called on countries to "finish the job".
Pointing to several recent deadly disease outbreaks, he stressed that completing a pandemic treaty was "about protecting people".
"A pathogen threat anywhere can become a threat everywhere, to people of every country," he said, according to a written version of his statement.
"The outbreak of hantavirus earlier this year, and the ongoing Ebola epidemic in DRC remind us of this threat."

He was referring to the hantavirus outbreak that killed three people on a cruise ship in April and the latest Ebola outbreak, declared in May, which has killed nearly 5,000 people out of more than 10,000 infected mostly in the DRC.
It was vital, Tedros said, that the world learn the overarching lesson of the Covid-19 pandemic: "no country can protect itself from pandemics by acting alone".
When countries agreed in May 2025 to a Pandemic Agreement, they left out the tricky issue of how the key mechanism would operate to get the deal over the line.

The agreement's Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system covers how to share access to pathogens with pandemic potential, as well as benefits derived from them such as vaccines, tests and treatments.
"PABS is the last remaining piece of our puzzle," Tedros said.
During the Covid pandemic, he highlighted that "the world developed vaccines in record time, but too many countries were left waiting while others secured far more than they needed".

articles.title: Vietnam scraps child organ donors proposal after backlash
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The newly revised draft still allows living minors to donate regenerative tissue, for bone marrow or stem cell transplants, to family members when no suitable adult donor is available
Vietnam withdrew on Monday a proposal allowing children aged 15 to 17 to donate their organs after death following public criticism in a country where deceased donor transplants remain limited.
The Southeast Asian country began kidney transplants in 1992 and performs the most annual transplants in the region, according to state media.
However, the vast majority of transplants in Vietnam rely on living donors. Transplants in many other nations mostly use organs from deceased donors, expanding their donor pool.
Officials in Vietnam say they are seeking to update a 2006 law on organ and tissue donation, aiming to increase life-saving transplants while safeguarding donors.

A draft submitted to the National Assembly last month proposed allowing 15- to 17-year-olds to donate their tissues, organs or bodies after death, provided the child's parent or legal representative consented.

But, after online backlash, officials removed the under-18 donor provision from a revised draft dated Sunday, with the government saying it had accepted recommendations from lawmakers that only legal adults should be permitted to donate their organs.
Dissent is heavily restricted in communist Vietnam, but opposition centred on whether parental consent could adequately protect child donors from pressure or exploitation.
Criticism also focused on a survey of schoolchildren as young as seven conducted in October to gather feedback on the draft law.
The poll prompted questions about whether minors could understand complex medical, legal and ethical issues, state outlet Tuoi Tre News said.
It said "the provision allowing minors to register as posthumous organ donors prompted considerable controversy and differing opinions among the public".
"Taking these concerns into account, the government has revised the draft," stipulating that only people aged 18 or older may donate their organs, Tuoi Tre said.
National Assembly deputy Pham Khanh Phong Lan urged lawmakers last month to oppose allowing child organ donors, saying: "You cannot sacrifice one child to save another."

articles.title: BJP rally leaves Hyderabad bus commuters stranded
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The mobilisation of crowds for Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s padayatra came at a cost to ordinary commuters on Monday, as the diversion of dozens of Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) buses for the BJP event left passengers waiting for long durations at bus stops across the city.

With the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) hiring city buses from several depots to ferry people to the rally, many commuters were forced to turn to the Metro Rail or wait for services that did not arrive. Those dependent on ordinary bus services, particularly pass holders, found their travel options limited.

Around 4 p.m. at Nampally, a stream of empty buses, decorated with BJP flags, headed towards the Exhibition Grounds after dropping off participants near the padayatra venue in Basheerbagh. At a bus shelter nearby, passengers watched the buses pass, hoping for a regular service to arrive.

“I left early today learning that buses would not be allowed on this route after some time. It looks like they have already been cancelled,” said Arunamma, a Class IV worker of a government office nearby.
A family with children and luggage waited at the same bus stop, hoping to catch a bus to Secunderabad. However, the services available were either SETWIN buses or higher-priced deluxe services.
“We have ordinary bus passes, but no ordinary bus has passed by for nearly half an hour,” said a female member of that family.
On a regular day, several services, including routes 8, 20, 5 and 49, connect the area to Secunderabad.
“A large number of city buses have been hired for the event. From our depot alone, 30 services were taken out,” said a driver from the Jeedimetla depot.
Attempts to contact TGSRTC officials to ascertain the total number of buses withdrawn from regular services did not elicit a response.
Meanwhile, the Red Line of the Hyderabad Metro, which connects L.B. Nagar and Miyapur, witnessed an unusually heavy rush, with several commuters opting for the trains to reach the event.

articles.title: Police must serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes: Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The observations were made while granting anticipatory bail to a 60-year-old Councillor, D. Sudha of the DMK, who had allegedly abused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay

The Madras High Court on Monday (November 2, 2026) disapproved of the practice of police registering criminal cases against all those who criticise or abuse the ruling party and said, the police personnel must remember that they “serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes.”

Justice N. Ramesh said that the police seldom register cases against ruling party members, irrespective of the party in power, on the basis of complaints lodged by the opposition. He wrote: “An even hand between the ruling party and its opponents is not a courtesy the police extend; it is a condition of their constitutional legitimacy.”

The observations were made while granting anticipatory bail to a 60-year-old Greater Chennai Corporation Councillor, D. Sudha of the DMK, who had allegedly abused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The judge agreed with her counsel, A. Damodaran, that the case does not require her arrest and consequent custodial interrogation.

Opining that initiation of criminal defamation proceedings would be the right course of action in cases of present nature, the judge said, an insult to a dignitary need not be converted into a public order crime so that the coercive machinery of cognisable investigation and threat of arrest could be deployed at once.

The judge said that the political discourse in the country was now conducted in substantial measure on social media, with all major political parties maintaining organised social media establishments, popularly called IT wings, whose daily work includes trolling and abusing the opponents.

The judge also referred to the incident in which Madras Institute of Development Studies (MIDS) Associate Professor A. articles.title: Sanction 2,000 Indiramma houses per Assembly constituency within a week: Telangana Housing MD
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Housing Department officials were directed to complete the sanctioning process of 2,000 Indiramma houses per Assembly constituency, under the second phase of the scheme, in a week’s time. First priority would be given to people living in huts.

With the success of the first phase of the housing project, people are eagerly waiting for the second phase, said the Corporation’s Managing Director V.P. Gautham. Selection process, remedies to delays in clearing bills for the beneficiaries, awareness of government facilitated cement bags and other aspects were discussed at a meeting with district project directors and deputy engineers, in Hyderabad on Monday (November 2, 2026).
Around 3.3 lakh houses were sanctioned under the first phase, and construction of around 2 lakh of them has been completed.

Mr. Gautham said that the State government issued guidelines for selection of beneficiaries who live in huts, which have to be adhered to. The officials were directed to allocate houses in coordination with public representatives and district in-charge ministers.

Awareness has to be created among people about the facility created by the government for the beneficiaries to buy cement at lower prices. The project directors were asked to inform people of the option to self-upload photos (of the houses) online to avoid delays in getting bills cleared.

articles.title: Anbumani opposes proposed ₹5 hike in Aavin milk prices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pointing out that Aavin milk was considerably cheaper than products sold by private dairies, he said a ₹5 increase would amount to a hike of up to 12.5%

PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss has urged the Tamil Nadu government to reject Aavin’s reported proposal to increase milk prices by ₹5 per litre, stating that it would place an additional burden on poor and middle-class families.

In a statement, he said the proposed hike followed a recent ₹6 per litre increase in the procurement price of milk supplied to Aavin, which was expected to widen the cooperative’s losses. Acknowledging that Aavin incurred a loss of ₹89.80 crore in 2025-26, he said increasing retail prices was not the only way to address its financial difficulties.

Pointing out that Aavin milk was considerably cheaper than products sold by private dairies, he said a ₹5 increase would amount to a hike of up to 12.5%. He called for addressing administrative inefficiencies and corruption in Aavin’s management and providing government subsidies to compensate for losses incurred in supplying milk at affordable prices.

articles.title: Clean energy investments helped India soften West Asia crisis impact: PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Inaugurating Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo, Narendra Modi says India’s economy continued to grow despite the crisis; warns that excess dependence on fossil fuels could risk increased exposure to global disruptions

The impact of the West Asia crisis on India would have been more severe than the rest of the world had the country not made investments in renewable energy over the last decade, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said at the inauguration of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (2026) in New Delhi Monday (November 2, 2026).

“Had India not made the investments it did in clean energy and building the requisite mechanisms [and infrastructure], the impact of the crisis would have been far more severe than in the rest of the world,” Mr. Modi said in his address. He also said that India’s economy continued to grow despite the crisis.
The Prime Minister put forth that the West Asia crisis exemplified how energy security was directly tied to economic security, adding that the future of energy security rested in clean energy.
He warned that excess dependence on fossil fuels could risk increased exposure to global disruptions.
Mr. Modi also said that India’s renewable energy sector would have investment opportunities of about $220 billion by the end of the decade.

In his pitch to potential investors, Mr. Modi held that it would be difficult to find the scale, scope and demand that India has in any other part of the world, alongside political and policy stability.
Mr. Modi emphasised that the next phase of solar revolution would rest on innovation.
He pointed to opportunities in the realm of indigenous manufacturing of essential hardware and battery storage systems, as well as in enhancing storage capacities.

Explaining his vision, the Prime Minister said, “We must carve out a dynamic where the country’s middle class has the option of an electric vehicle, and where they would be able to charge their scooty, bike, or car with solar-based energy. This would help save them a lot of money.”
He said the country would also require solutions that would help spur solar adoption in the dairy sector, animal husbandry, and farming.
Mr. Modi observed that India’s solar module manufacturing has grown from 2 gigawatts (GW) to 200 GW in a decade with the capacity to manufacture solar cells having grown to about 40 GW.
“Now we are working on enhancing [indigenous] manufacturing of other components as well,” he said.

articles.title: Congress seeks JPC probe into IDBI Bank sale, alleges valuation irregularities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The party questions the use of bank’s funds by Fairfax to finance acquisition; demands disclosure of valuation reports

The Congress on Monday (November 2, 2026) demanded an immediate halt to the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings and a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) probe into the transaction, alleging that the government had manipulated the bank’s valuation.
The party alleged that the foreign buyer would use the bank’s own funds to finance the acquisition.

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh separately described the transaction as a “major scam” by the Narendra Modi government and demanded that both valuation reports be made public.
Addressing a press conference, senior Congress leader Shaktisinh Gohil alleged that the disinvestment process was riddled with irregularities and lacked transparency.

Citing a conversation between an analyst and Fairfax Chairman Prem Watsa and President Peter Clarke, Mr. Gohil claimed that the company had indicated that the payment would be made in instalments, with the initial investment followed by the use of IDBI Bank’s resources to meet the remaining acquisition cost.
“Prem Watsa is a very close to Modi ji and had showered praise on him during the 2017 Vibrant Gujarat Summit,” the Congress leader said.

Mr. Gohil questioned the rationale of selling a profitable Indian bank to a foreign company using its own funds. He said IDBI Bank had earned a cumulative profit of ₹30,105 crore between 2021 and 2026 and had non-performing assets of only about 2%.
Its profit per employee stood at ₹49.8 lakh, making it one of the leading banks on this measure, he said. “Why is a bank that is delivering such high profits being sold?” he asked.

The Congress leader also questioned the revision of the bank’s valuation from ₹94.42 to ₹75 a share after the bids had been opened. He said the government had initially fixed the valuation at ₹94.42 a share before inviting bids, but subsequently revised it downwards.
The government was now claiming to have secured a good deal by selling the bank at ₹81 a share, he said, demanding disclosure of both valuation reports and the identity of the second bidder.

Mr. Gohil invoked an assurance given by the then Finance Minister Jaswant Singh in Parliament in August 2003 that the government’s stake in IDBI Bank would not be reduced below 51%. A Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance had also favoured retaining the government’s majority stake, he said.

He further questioned the regulatory concessions extended to Fairfax, including the two-year window reportedly allowed to reduce its control in another Indian bank, and sought details of the source of funds for the acquisition.

articles.title: Capex push to continue, but fiscal prudence non-negotiable: FM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: “India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism says Ms. Sitaraman

Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to sustaining capital expenditure (capex) to support economic growth, while stressing that fiscal prudence would remain non-negotiable.

“Capex is a very important component of our growth strategy. Because till such time the private sector will be able to expand capacity or make capital investment, it is important for the Government to push through with capital investment,” she said at an event organised by HSBC India in Mumbai.
Pointing to the returns from public investment over the past four to five years, she said the multiplier effects had strengthened the Government’s confidence in continuing the spending push.

“We find that in the last 4 to 5 years, we have got very good success. The multipliers actually work and it gives us confidence that the Government is not going to sit back and watch whether growth is growing without doing much,” she said.

The Government would be willing to extend capex support to ensure that the growth momentum was not disrupted. “We will continue doing that because India’s growth momentum should not be lost at all,” she said.
However, Ms. Sitharaman made it clear that higher public spending would have to be balanced against fiscal constraints.
“We need to be fiscally prudent,” she said, adding that while some advocated spending without worrying about sovereign credit ratings, responsible expenditure was essential.
“I agree we need to spend but it has to be done responsibly and fiscal prudence will be our top priority,” she emphasised.
“We have to be prudent and we have to be creative based on which we can encourage growth and stability,” she added.
The Finance Minister also called for greater confidence in India’s economic prospects, urging businesses and experts to move beyond pessimism and sector-specific concerns.

“India must to talk with optimism and there needs to be reduction in cynicism,” she said, questioning why experts who considered their own sectors healthy remained apprehensive about the broader economy.
“If your sector doing fine, others sectors in India must be similarly fine. So can the narrate and language change?” she asked.

articles.title: No-cost EMI: a loan that is portrayed as free
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays.

Every festive season, the same board greets you at the electronics shop: “No-cost EMI”. TVs, washing machines and appliances are available at no-cost EMI. A ₹60,000 phone, 6 easy instalments of ₹10,000, no interest. It feels as if the shopkeeper has done you a favour. He has not. Nobody lends money for free and nobody sells at a loss. Someone pays. Lets see who.

A bank or finance firm funds the purchase and charges interest. The shop agrees to bear interest but it will recover it in one of two ways. Either the price quoted to you is higher, or you lose the discount a cash buyer would have got Take the same phone. A cash buyer gets it for ₹57,000. The EMI buyer pays ₹60,000. The ₹3,000 gap is the interest.

articles.title: In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda

Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since Prime Minister Balendra Shah took charge in March this year following the election that was conducted under an interim government. A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.

“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.

Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the agrément (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to the disaster in Bhote Koshi river is also expected to be on the agenda.

Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. The India visit by Mr. Shah, if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli.

In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati.

Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” said Mr. Lamichhane before starting the visit.

articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed good faith

Iran on Monday (November 2, 2026) said it was ready to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington agrees to conditions, as U.S. President Donald Trump issued his latest war threat at a rally for midterm elections.
A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed "good faith".

Tehran has blockaded Hormuz since the war started in February, sending energy prices soaring and posing an electoral challenge for Trump. The narrow gateway to the energy-rich Gulf normally carries one-fifth of global oil consumption.
"The possibility of implementing this plan in two days is another indication of Iran's good-faith approach," Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told reporters at a briefing.
"We have stated that, if Iran's demands are met, it would be possible to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz and resume the negotiating process within a short period."

In September, Iran proposed a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz if the U.S. agreed to demands including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending its counter-blockade of Iranian ports.
Mr. Baqaei said messages were being exchanged with the United States via mediators, adding that "everything depends" on the U.S. side accepting the Iranian demands.
During final rallies for the U.S. midterms on Tuesday (November 3), where diesel prices and consumer inflation are a key issue, Trump struck a belligerent tone, warning Iran to expect "the hammer".

"The only reason why I'm not finished with Iran is I want to be nice. I want to try and save all those lives if I can... But at some point we're going to have to give them the hammer," he told voters in Iowa.
Officials from Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Turkey have held talks with Iran in recent days, while U.S. Vice President JD Vance sent a letter to Tehran.
Oman's ruler Sultan Haitham bin Tariq discussed the war with Chinese President Xi Jinping during a visit to Beijing on Monday (November 2), an Omani foreign ministry statement said.

"The two sides called for resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, urging the United States and Iran to pursue a peaceful path, achieve a ceasefire (and) prevent war entirely," it said, calling for "dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible".

articles.title: U.K. warns EU against keeping Britain out of ‘Made in Europe’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money
U.K. Defence Minister Wes Streeting on Monday (November 1, 2026) warned the EU against keeping Britain out of its "Made in Europe" industrial push, weeks before a key EU-U.K. summit.

The European Union wants to boost domestic sectors like cars and defence by forcing companies to buy European if they want public money, but the efforts have raised concerns in London about the U.K.'s potential exclusion.

"We need to be careful" to avoid that the Made in Europe push "doesn't spread into self-defeating protectionism", Streeting said alongside top EU diplomat Kaja Kallas ahead of their talks in Brussels.
The British Minister will also meet EU Defence Chief Andrius Kubilius.
Monday's (November 2) talks come just over two weeks before EU chiefs and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham will meet for a summit in Brussels on November 20.
Mr. Burnham has said the long-awaited meeting would be a chance to start a "serious dialogue" about long-term relations between the U.K. and the bloc, a decade after the Brexit vote to leave.
One of the major issues on the table this month will be "Made in Europe" even though it is not officially on the summit's agenda.

As the EU's push to cut dependence on non-EU companies widens to include artificial intelligence development and cloud computing, the U.K. fears new digital rules being prepared will also exclude British companies.
London and Brussels hope to clinch deals on food and drink trade, youth mobility and avoiding EU carbon emissions taxes during the November 20 talks.
The EU hopes to make progress especially on cutting the fees EU students have to pay to attend British universities.
The bloc's capitals will discuss the draft of a joint EU-U.K. summit statement during a meeting of ambassadors Wednesday in Brussels.
Streeting will also meet German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius later on Monday (November 2) in Berlin.

articles.title: Jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine on board and leaving a fiery crater
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration
All nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood, U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday (November 1, 2026).

The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Duffy said the Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board's investigation into the cause.

The Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood on Sunday (November 1, 2026) and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes before crashing near a busy roadway, creating a giant fiery crater in the pavement.
Roads remain closed after a Learjet 60 believed to be carrying nine people crashed in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, on November 1, 2026. | Photo Credit: Reuters

The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration. Authorities did not immediately say what caused the jet to go down or who was on it.
Jim Reynolds, a spokesperson for Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, said it was a private aircraft. He could not immediately provide details about who was on the flight.

Video shot from people inside their cars captured the terrifying moment the aircraft plunged from the sky, before striking near the roadway and exploding. Flames flickered around chunks of pavement lining the crater as people milled about, expressing shock it landed only feet from homes and only inches from passing vehicles. Thick black smoke engulfed the crash site.
It was unclear if the crash caused any damage to homes.

The crash occurred near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North. The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office closed roads in both directions and urged motorists to avoid the area. Firefighters and other emergency personnel rushed to the scene.
A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: A woman working nearby said electricity in the area had been out for approximately two hours following the crash.

articles.title: Japan urges U.S. to enforce discipline after second Marine arrest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The case has triggered outrage in Japan and reignited controversy over the heavy U.S. military presence on the southern island

Japan urged the United States to enforce discipline among its troops after a Marine was arrested on suspicion of drink driving during a curfew in the wake of another serviceman's arrest on a murder charge, the Defence Minister said on Monday (November 2, 2026).

U.S. forces on the Japanese island of Okinawa were barred from drinking alcohol for two days early last month and faced a 30-day curfew after the murder of a woman allegedly committed by an American Marine.
The case has triggered outrage in Japan and reignited controversy over the heavy U.S. military presence on the southern island.
A second Marine had been arrested over allegations he drove under the influence of alcohol, Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said.
The arrest took place on Saturday, according to media reports.

"We requested that the U.S. side strictly enforce discipline among its personnel, implement effective measures to prevent a recurrence, and ensure full compliance with the nighttime curfew," Mr. Koizumi told reporters.
"We want them to take (the incident) seriously," he added.
The curfew imposed last month required all troops to be back on base or at "an off-base domicile" from midnight to 5:00 am.
Last week, Japanese prosecutors indicted the Marine accused of murdering a woman in Okinawa.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi told lawmakers days after the woman's death that the government had lodged a strong protest with the United States, urging their "full cooperation with the investigation" and "strict discipline among U.S. military personnel".
The Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper reported that, according to the indictment document, the 20-year-old suspect allegedly strangled the woman from Naha in a hotel with a telephone cord on October 3.
The United States has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

articles.title: Foreign policy is a local issue in U.S. midterm campaigns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The number of Republicans who say that Trump’s policies have made the economy worse has almost doubled (18% to 35%) since the start of the year

As Americans vote to elect new lawmakers on Capitol Hill and at State and local levels on November 3, foreign policy issues have become enmeshed in domestic policy issues. Specifically, these issues are U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs on trading partners, the war in Iran and, to a lower extent U.S. support for Israel. The Iran war caused gas and diesel prices to shoot up. This, along with tariffs, has created problems for Republicans in their strongholds and challenges for Mr. Trump with his own base of manufacturing workers, business owners and farmers.

Between September 1 and October 14, campaign ads for at least half of 50 competitive Senate and House races featured Iran, according to a study by the Associated Press. The total spend on these ads was $ 42 million. Almost all the 65 unique ads, according to the AP study, linked the Iran war to the cost of living.
